oe1bu9454-001.notes: The Prince writes to Triebenfeld (in Vienna, at the Congress). He has heard from a friend that Austria, Russia and Prussia have agreed on Saxony and Poland, and he has had no news from Triebenfeld since 13 January. He urges Triebenfeld to get Hardenberg to grant the 112000 Rthl advance and put the Majorat estates under administration, which would end Cosmar's power. A mandatary has promised to hand over the debt instrument for 12000 Rthl in cash and a secure assignment on 100000. The favourable report of the Brieg Oberlandesgericht has been sent in. Triebenfeld should also pursue the Trąbczyn and Kamionna matter: the King granted these estates, the Poles took them away, and the Kaiser should order their return. Several words are garbled.

oe1bu9454-001a.notes: Triebenfeld, in Vienna, sends the Prince a letter he has just received from the "so höchst bedrängten Fürsten von Hohenlohe" and describes that prince's terrible need. He pleads for the advance of 112000 rt. With it the Curland heirs would be paid off, Cosmar's hold on the Majorat estates would end, His Majesty would get the money back from the Majorat funds, and the creditors would be paid. The other prince's letter mentions the Trąbczyn estates in Konin district. Triebenfeld asks whether he may now submit the deeds and documents. Several words are garbled (lines 4-5, 7-8, 10, 12).

Sr Majestät erhalte die 112000 Rthl aus den Fonds der Majoratsgüter zurück, und die Gläubiger würden nach und nach bezahlt.
Zu den Trąbczyner Gütern im Kreis Konin, die im Schreiben erwähnt werden, erbittet er Weisung, ob er jetzt die Urkunden und Dokumente einreichen darf.

oe1bu9454-002.notes: Triebenfeld schreibt aus Wien während des Kongresses an Fürst Friedrich Ludwig. Er ist bestürzt, dass der Fürst seit dem 13. keine Briefe erhalten haben will, und zählt auf, was in seinen 7 Briefen stand: General Schöler wegen Trąbczyn, Dank an Stägemann, die Güterkreise fallen an Russland, Sachsen. Er fleht um 200 Ducaten, weil er dem Staatskanzler 100 und Barbe 70 schuldet. Die Akten liegen bei Stägemann, das Geld werde gezahlt und ein Administrator angestellt. Pourtalès will in der Sache „Ko:“ kaufen, hat aber vorerst nur 150/m bar. Kongressgerüchte. Fürst August soll Cosmars Vollmacht sofort widerrufen und den Widerruf den Gerichten mitteilen.

oe1bu9454-003.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna, apparently February 1815, to Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen. He has had only two letters from him (19 and 28 Jan). He is in desperate need of money: he reckoned on 1400 rt per 4 weeks but has received only 932 rt in 5 months, and he owes "dem Fürsten und Barben" 170 #. With Barbe he is going to Nesselrode and Schröder about the Polish matter. He asks urgently for 200 #. He advises the Prince to send a Pro Memoria proposing a trustworthy administrator of the Majorat estates for the King's account, and lists the qualities that man needs. He hopes for the Fürst's resolution on the advance and the Polish estates.

oe1bu9454-004.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna to the Prince. News of Napoleon's return: Grenoble taken, about 30,000 men, a bounty of 10 million francs on his head. Requests: a Korbwagen for Hoffrath Barbe's servant, who is to go from Sławięcice to Switzerland to fetch Barbe's sister; a cart with 2 horses to bring glass from Prague for the Hofräte Barbe, Heym and Philipsborn; a pass for his own two men back to Blizanow. He wants Eberhard to come and is indignant at Eberhard's demand for a Vorspann pass and travel costs. He asks what Fürst August did about the Vollmacht and wants more Blanquets. The postscript covers conflicting rumours and fear of Napoleon's appeal to the lower classes. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-005.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Blizanow. Zerboni has asked Trzciński to pay him, citing an alleged cession of the Prince's claim of 10000 r. and 5000 r. Triebenfeld disputes this and asks for quick information. Trzciński also says he paid 1000 to König for the Bischdorf business on Zerboni's instruction; Triebenfeld calls it a swindle and fears the Prince may have given Zerboni a blank signed sheet. Prefect v Smiedecki in Kalisz has been won over and will report favourably in the compensation matter concerning Sokolnik. Triebenfeld awaits answers on Betsche and other matters. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-006.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna to the Prince, sending the letter with Prinz Adolph, who is leaving. He reports on two matters. The first is compensation in the Russian share: he has demanded the Starostei Sokolnik with Wieruszew, set against the Prince's claim, with Stein and Nesselrode handling it. The second is the Curische affair: Albrecht, the King, Stägemann, a settlement with the Curische Erben, and Cosmar's mismanagement. He sends his and Albrecht's plan as an enclosure. He also covers Hardenberg's empty promises, Pourtalès and Adolph's business, begs for 100 Ducaten by Estaffette and complains about F. August, enclosing a Langenburg letter. The middle section, lines 28-41, is florid and partly garbled. Nothing concerns Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Entschädigung im russischen Anteil; Starostei Sokolnik mit Wieruszew gefordert, verrechnet mit der Forderung des Fürsten
claims.why: Z. 8 nennt das Dedomagement im russischen Anteil, Z. 12-13 sagen, die Starostei Sokolnik sei gefordert und werde mit der Forderung des Fürsten kompensiert. Die Verbindung zu Wieruszew steht aber im entstellten Wort 'ohnmit' (wohl 'ohnweit', also nahe Wieruszew). 'mit Wieruszew' legt dieses Wort aus, und es ist nicht belegt, dass Wieruszew mitgefordert wurde.

oe1bu9454-007.notes: Charlotte von Triebenfeld, the daughter of the agent, writes to the Prince from Breslau. It is her third letter and none has been answered. A letter from her father has again pointed her to the Prince's grace. She is in great misery. She no longer asks for help, only for her father's address, which one of the Prince's subordinates could send her. The letter has nothing to do with Trąbczyn. The text is sound, with a few doubtful endings and a doubtful closing verb in line 22.

oe1bu9454-008.notes: Short, desperate note from Triebenfeld (Vienna, December 1814) to the Prince. He has received three letters (8, 25 and 27 November). Letters from his children leave him close to despair. He asks for 120 Rthl for the children and 60 Rthl a month while he stays. He lives on borrowed money. He says the Prince's affair stands well. He asks for a small written promise from the Curische Mandatarius that the matter will be settled for 112/m Rthl. He speaks of powerful enemies (passage garbled). He will write to Hahn. He needs no papers except a few words from the Mandatarius. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-010.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna to Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen. He acknowledges the Prince's letter of the 24th of last month and is astonished that his own letters, sent twice a week and mostly via Teichelmann, have not arrived; he will have a Laufzettel sent after them. Stägemann has still made no report, but the Fürst Kanzler has given good assurances. Triebenfeld has handed the Polish matter to the Commission with a pro memoria and expects estates rather than money. He passes on war news and rumours, says the Württemberg affair should end well, is surprised at Fürst August's delay in revoking the Vollmacht, and encloses a letter for Eberhard.

oe1bu9454-011.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna during the Congress. He says the Prince's affair is to be decided this week. He urges that Eberhard be sent at once to settle with the heirs ("Churp. Erbinen"). If needed, the estates would be administered 5 years longer, and a pension of 10-12/m or 6/m rt is mentioned. Congress news: Saxony, Württemberg, Russia in Poland. He is outraged that Fürst August will not take the power of attorney back from Cosmar. He proposes a step for Prinz Adolph through Hardenberg (the key word "Magirenn" is garbled) and asks for 100 # to pay Barbe. Postscript: rumour that the Austrian army is being put on a war footing. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-012.notes: This is a short, urgent note or postscript from Triebenfeld (probably in Vienna) to the Prince. He begs for "die 200 #" (the currency sign is unclear). Without money nothing can be done in Vienna, and everything would be lost. The Prince should make sure Fürst August quickly takes the power of attorney back from Cosmar. People in Vienna think poorly of the young gentleman. The Prince should watch out for the Revers he gave, which the Prince seems to have left in Öhringen. On Württemberg: the King has recognised the mediatised as Stände and sent a draft constitution, and the Stände have protested. The text breaks off at the end. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-013.notes: This is a confidential letter from Triebenfeld, in Vienna, to the Prince, on two pages. It criticises how the matter was taken down in the protocol, including the Adolph affair. "Hahn" (H) wants Adolph freed and declared of age by the King so that he can buy Koschentin. It compares the yields of Koschentin and Schlawenschitz. On his own affairs: paper money is losing value, he owes Barbe 145 #, he needs clothes, and he asks for 200 # and 2 blank sheets signed in French. The Fürst is giving him an advance of 100 #. Page 2: no letter for 3½ weeks, and he is living on bread and water. Barbe will raise money to redeem the papers. There are hopes for help from the King, but that passage is garbled. A new translator will do the Acten for 15 Ducaten. There is still no answer from Pourtalès. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-014.notes: A letter to a "Freund" who is about to come back from Vienna, signed Eberhard at line 28. The metadata gives sender and recipient as not identified, so the summary says "der Schreiber". Points: why has the Staats Kanzler (garbled at line 2) not acted on the Prince's complaint; private news from Berlin of an investigation against Cosmar, which the writer thinks would do harm; the Karl/Curische debt, which could not be settled; a request that the King take the debt over; the 35000 Rthl the Prince owes the King. A postscript in another hand speaks of Eberhard in the third person and calls the news a Schreckschuss. There is nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Der Schreiber fragt, warum auf die Beschwerde des Fürsten noch nichts verfügt sei.

Ein Vergleich über die Schuld ist gescheitert: Die Generalmandatarien lehnen ab, weil Justizrath Henneberg in Berlin beschieden wurde, die Sache auszusetzen.
Der König soll die Schuld nicht nur vorschießen, sondern ganz übernehmen und dem Fürsten auch die 35000 Rthl erlassen.
claims.why: Lines 18-19 ask that the King take over the debt entirely. On the 35000 rth the Fürst owes the King, line 21 only says they might well also be cancelled ('wohl auch erlaßen werden dürfte'). It is an expectation, not a demand.

oe1bu9454-015.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna to Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen. First he reports business. Fürst August's claim to 100000 rt, a legacy of Fürstin Sakkin: the Staats Kanzler writes to Öhringen that the King has no objection, and Kircheisen is instructed. The Prince's case lies with Stägemann. The advance of 112000 rt counts as successful. Cosmar's removal is decided. On the Polish affairs, the Posen items will be easy to obtain, but the Trąbczyn matter faces great difficulties. The files are in Polish and must be translated, and the sworn translator wants 260 fl, which Triebenfeld lacks. Then he describes his own misery: ill, penniless, owing Barbe 70 #. Beguelin will press the Chancellor and Stägemann. Nothing has come from the Prince since 7 Feb. He asks for support for his daughter.

oe1bu9454-016.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna to Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen. Rumours about when the monarchs will leave keep changing; he encloses a Nota. He asked Obristlieutenant v Thiel whether the King will still be in Vienna when Prinz Adolph arrives on the 20th. Thiel said the King would be glad and that they would not leave before the 22nd. He has not yet spoken to Hardenberg, and the Prince's affairs are still stuck. War news: Murat has reached Mantua, the Russians are marching, Bonaparte is massing troops at Paris. The end of the letter is garbled: some estate business, an equivalent owed to the Prince, creditors, and a hypothec on Zagorowo in the writer's favour.

oe1bu9454-017.notes: Pro Memoria from Triebenfeld to the Prince. General Kleist asked Prefect Garczynski in Kalisz about the Hohenlohe estates. Kleist said the Prince's sons had told him in Berlin that Triebenfeld pockets all the income. Triebenfeld defends himself: Cabanis, Hecker, Honrichs and the sequestrators managed the estates, and Cabanis is now laying his account before Komornik Chomanowski. He gives figures for the interest arrears. He complains that Sommer has spread rumours about the Prince's debts and asks that Sommer not be sent again. He asks for a quick answer on Sobottendorff, Weigel and the Invaliden sum, and for the Anweisung on the French decree and the original receipt. Much of the text is garbled.

oe1bu9454-018.notes: Triebenfeld, ill with fever at Blizanow, writes to the Prince. He objects to the instrument and power of attorney the Prince sent, since he already holds a general power of attorney. The Invaliden Casse has put everything under arrest. While he was held by the French in Berlin he had to pay the Prince's debt, and the French General Direction ordered 3121 rt plus costs and interest repaid to him from the estates. He claims 4219 rt and dictates the declaration the Prince should issue, on the Komornik's advice: the sum is to be assigned to him from the interest arrears of the inhabitants of Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica, Kopojno and other places, collectable by execution. He sends his forester and needs the instrument by the 15th or 16th.

oe1bu9454-019.notes: This is Triebenfeld's appendix ("Anhang") to doc 18 of the same date. He pushes a plan to pay off Sobottendorff, whom the Prince owes 40000 rt, through an 18-year lease. He has come to terms with Tschachmann or Cybalski and with Hawich, and will give Hawich a mortgage on his own Blizanow for 1300 rt Abstand. He will lease the lands, buildings and meadows to Sobottendorff for 36000 rt. He urges haste and asks for the instrument exactly as he drafted it, because everything is under arrest. He needs 300 rt for the Warsaw lawsuit. He expects news on the Witów lawsuit, which would bring 4000 rt. He complains about expenses and hardship. The text is garbled in places.

oe1bu9454-021.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Konotop late at night to the Prince, covering a second messenger sent to Lombardini after the Estaffette sent at noon. Dlugo Lędcki visited; people fear the Russians will come soon. Every Pole expects the Prince to recover the Trąbczyn, Kaemen and Brzyce estates. There is a garbled plan about Constantin, Lowicz and Talleyrand, then garbled gossip (Dorothechen, "die alte Ziege" in Paris). He asks for a quick answer and for money to bribe and to work; Richter has pawned his watch. Konotop and Schweinern are leased for 14000 rt a year, and old arrears take everything until Johanni. He is waiting for the Urkunde and the money; Honrichs is waiting to leave with Stenger. Lombardini should give at least 200 rt Münze to his daughters in Breslau.

oe1bu9454-022.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Konotop. He is ill with gout. He complains of four lawsuits he has to carry because he stood surety for the Prince: the Invaliden Casse, Oppenheimer, and Obrist Schliefen (Breslau). In Poland he is suing Meierowitz, who owes Schliefen 6000 rt purchase money for Wittow and owes the Prince 500 rt a year in Erbzins, 2500 rt in arrears. He has hired Stenger. He is expecting Honrichs and Hawich, and calls Hawich the greatest rogue; a Badenski appointed by the government collects all the money. Lombardini did not pay the 150 rt for his son and daughters. He asks for 500 rt Münze for his children and would repay 1000 at Johanni. He will present his account once he is well.

Lahr and Coste; money still owed to Lahr and to Blochsdorff/Holzapfel). He lists his hardships: distraint, gout, hunger. Criminal Rath Stenger from Kargowa is to put things in order in Zagórów, Trąbczyn, Pszczew and Witów, recover Trąbczyn and Kamionna, and wants to hire an actuary Seifert. Triebenfeld lists the pending lawsuits and mentions a rumour that the Russians will occupy Poland. In the postscript Honrichs faces arrest over three Vorwerke, and Lombardini has not paid the 150 rt.

oe1bu9454-024.notes: This is a request signed "F. L. f. z. Hohenlohe" (lines 31-33) to an unnamed Geheimer Rath. Because the colonisation of Zagórów and Trąbczyn has produced a net yield of 40247 rt, confirmed by the Kalisz chamber, the writer asks the addressee to arrange a single loan of 400000 rt. The loan would pay all his debts and be secured by a first mortgage on both estates. A power of attorney and the documents are to follow, and a fee is promised. Three enclosures follow: a list of the places in both estates; a yield statement signed v Triebenfeld (Erbzinsen from the colonies 16781 rt); and a list of the Prince's debts totalling 366000, which includes Prusimska at about 16000. Sender and recipient are given as not identified, so the summary does not name them.

oe1bu9454-025.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Berlin. He had to rush to Zagorowo because the peasants had risen again and would not accept the separation of the lands; that matter is now settled. The King and Triebenfeld's patron have left Berlin, so he has found money another way: Justiz Rath Bucholz manages 80000 rt belonging to a von Bredow, to be lent on mortgages on Kontop, Schweinern and Trąbczyn and paid out to Schlabrendorff, Weigel, Hahn, the Prince and for the Wulffen debt. Separately, Tismar (Tesmar) is negotiating a loan of 360000 rt with Nathusius in Magdeburg. Land sales are slow because of the war, but Honrichs reports new buyers at the higher prices.

oe1bu9454-026.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince after the army's defeat in 1806. Secretair Koppe has told him the Prince survived. Minister von Stein lent him 8000 Rthl on the Konotop mortgage of 10000 Rthl. False reports led him towards Sagan. Now he sends a 6000 Rthl draft on Breslau to Koppe and will bring 4000 Rthl more. He will ask Stein for money on the Schweinern mortgage of 20000 Rthl. He has heard from the Cabinet that the Prince's bravery is praised and hopes the Prince will receive the Kolziger Güter, which would bring 100000 Rthl. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-027.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Breslau. The Prusimski family has taken Trąbczyn and Kaemen (Kamionna) by force. He has only lodged protests to secure the sum registered in his name, and expects them to be rejected for now. Generalin v. Sanitz has written to Napoleon about her husband's estates (lines 22-23 garbled), and her answer is to serve as the norm for the Prince's case. He is leaving for Memel tomorrow, perhaps going on to Petersburg, and hopes for help from Alexander or Grand Duke Constantin. The King and Queen revere the Prince but cannot help. Several garbled words in the passage from line 18 to line 43.

oe1bu9454-028.notes: Hawich schreibt aus Pyzdry an den Fürsten. Die Trąbczyner Güter sind am 3. d. Übergeben wurden sie an Canonicus v Jezierski, den Generalbevollmächtigten der Frau v Dąbska geb. v Prusimska. Hawich hat protestiert und sich dabei auf den Tilsiter Frieden berufen. Er hat eine Abschrift der Verordnung erbeten und die Rechte wegen der bezahlten Schulden vorbehalten. Dazu kommen zwei neue Prozesse: Probst Iwanski fordert den Decem von Swięcia. Otocki und der Müller Ekstaedt fordern etwa 7000 Rthl aus dem Trąbczyner Pachtvertrag von 1798. Hawich bittet, den in Breslau geschlossenen Vergleich zu schicken und eine Vollmacht zu erteilen.

oe1bu9454-029.notes: Bally writes from Sławięcice to Krieges Rath von Triebenfeld. At their meeting with Hoffrath Hahn in Łosiów near Brzeg, Triebenfeld promised a rendezvous, apparently after his return from Memel. Bally supposes he is back in Wrocław and asks whether and when he may call on him, because his gracious lord (Durchlaucht) has asked about it. He has heard that French troops are to be billeted in Sławięcice too, which would keep him from leaving, and it would be worse if he had to clear the stables. He hopes to speak with him soon. Nothing on Trąbczyn. Some garbled phrases: lines 6, 10, 17, 20.

Oppenheimer hatte die Zahlung übernommen, kaufte sich aber los. Zastrow bürgte für 5000 Rthl Papiergeld (ergab 2875 Rthl), die am 1. Juni in Courant zurückzuzahlen sind. oe1bu9454-033.notes: Triebenfeld, ill in Berlin, answers the Prince's letter of the 28th of last month. The transcription is rough. He is holding back letters to Kopey/Amelang. oe1bu9454-038.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Berlin. He is ill and keeps it short. He has received 3000 rt from the banker Veit and handed the Anweisung to Amelang. He explains his debts: 5176 rt of new debt, borrowed with Zastrow's help. Hecker's caution papers have lost value, and a total of 4209 rt cannot be raised in cash. Wood and boards from Konotop were taken instead of money, which pays off 4176 rt, and Zastrow has his papers back. He loses 3480 rt on the wood and asks to be reimbursed. He advises the Prince to raise 150000 rt, which would buy 750000 rt in papers and pay all debts. He plans to go to Vienna and perhaps Öhringen. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-039.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Berlin. He is back from "W:" and has settled his business there, but creditors are already threatening execution over 3000 rt he owes. He borrowed that money after getting out of French arrest in February. Of the 6125 rt owed, the Prince paid 3000 rt, which leaves 3125 rt. Nothing is coming in from Zagórów, so he wants the strictest execution requested from the French authority. He expects travel orders within 7 days and will probably go on to Königsberg. He wants guarantors, begs for at least 2000 rt, and asks that letters go to Justiz Commissarius Empich. He also reminds the Prince of the große Anlehn. The letter says nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-040.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. He fears letters are being intercepted. His travel plan has changed: first Wien, then back via Königsberg to Holland and Paris, with a visit to Öhringen. His loan plan: 250000 Rthl on the Zagórów mortgage would buy 750000 Rthl in papers. An advance of 46000 Rthl is needed for Oppenheimer, the Invaliden Casse and Meyer Bernhard. He advises buying Seehandlung bonds to repay the King. He mentions enemies at court and Stein. He is short of money: he borrowed 4000 Rthl in Münze to pay von der Lahr. The French government has promised military help to collect the Zagórów arrears. The subjects refuse to pay interest because of a Saxon ban.

oe1bu9454-042.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. French gendarmerie arrested him as the Prince's plenipotentiary to force payment of 3521 rt interest arrears to the Invaliden Casse. oe1bu9454-043.notes: Triebenfeld, writing from Kontop, tells the Prince that Amelang has reported a judgment: Lahr is to get his remaining 3000 rt in cash rather than in papers. Because it is a bill-of-exchange case, Triebenfeld faces arrest if he neither pays nor deposits the sum. Amelang has appealed, and he and Grevenitz expect to win, which would save about 1500 rt. By order of the French General Government the Lahr money is to be refunded, and the sequestration is to be lifted once about 10000 Rthl of interest has been paid. Hawich has been summoned. The Oppenheimer case is going well. Triebenfeld has a contract with Michaelis for 600 Centner of iron, for which he received 2000 rt, and asks the Prince to supply the iron. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-044.notes: Triebenfeld to Prince Hohenlohe, 3 Feb 1809. The Lahr lawsuit keeps him where he is. The judgment Amelang reported gives Lahr 3000 rt plus interest, but Lahr has to take papers; Triebenfeld's pledged obligations must be redeemed. He has returned to Coste the 9000 rt deposited against Lahr's 5000 rt, paid 450 rt interest and 118 rt to the bookkeeper and the broker Oldekopp, and comes to 2068 rt. He says the French Gouvernement ordered this money repaid from the Zagórów estates. Michaelis offers to settle the 2068 rt if the Prince delivers 600 Centner of iron at 4 rt free to Opole by May. Triebenfeld also asks for 932 rt in outlays (521 for the Oppenheimer suit and messengers, 411 for the gendarmerie).

oe1bu9454-046.notes: Amelang writes from Berlin to Triebenfeld. The Prince's letter, with the money attached, should by now have reached Triebenfeld; it was drawn on Kontop. A case lies in the appeal court awaiting judgment, but Amelang expects no favourable outcome. The reason is a royal declaration printed in the Berlin newspapers: bonds must be repaid in Courant even when the Valuta was paid in state papers, back to 1806. The passage on interest rates is garbled. Amelang sympathises with Triebenfeld. The text is a rough transcription. The next letter (doc 20) shows the matter is the van der Lahr debt, but this letter does not name it.

oe1bu9454-047.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kontop to a Hoffrath (Wohlgeborner Herr; the edition gives the Prince as recipient) and refers to the Prince in the third person. Hawich and Hecker came from Zagórów, and a report went to the Prince by express. He answers four points. (1) The Saxon moratorium and the Invaliden Casse's 50000 Rthl first mortgage: only interest needs paying; Honrichs, as sequestrator, has handed the money over; lawsuits against Oppenheimer are running in Berlin and Kalisz. (2) Meyer's claim for building work is unknown to him; Meyer was never in the Prince's service; Giese and consorts owe 25000 Rthl, under lawsuit. (3) Niedźwiecki: a lawsuit is pending. (4) The Augustinow colonists' petition for remission is to be refused. He cannot travel to Schlawenschitz: debts, and his Kontop estates are sequestrated.

oe1bu9454-048.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kontop to Prince Hohenlohe. He had Hawich, the Justiz Bürgermeister of Zagórów, and Ober Inspector Hecker with him and issued thirteen special powers of attorney. They cover the rejection of Dąbska's claim to Trąbczyn, lifting the sequestration, collecting interest, a suit against Oppenheimer et Wolff, removing Honrichs as sequester and annulling his land sales, arrears from Niedźwiecki, the Oleśnica tenants, boundary suits, the Warsaw Reichstag, the Invaliden Casse and the Radzinski heirs. The acts were recorded by Schenck. A second copy (doc 302) differs in some figures and names.

oe1bu9454-050.notes: This is a petition from the Prince to King Friedrich Wilhelm III. In 1808 the Prince owed the Invaliden Casse 3125 rt in interest on a 50000 rt capital secured on the Zagórów estates. The French government, which had taken over that fund, forced the money out of Triebenfeld in Berlin by arrest and military execution. To pay it, Triebenfeld borrowed 5140 rt in paper money from van der Lahr on a joint bill with Zastrow. The Prince sent 3000 rt; van der Lahr sued for the rest, won a judgment and threatens execution. Amelang is to settle: 1000 rt in cash and the rest in iron by May. Van der Lahr has accepted, apart from the iron price. The Prince asks the King to spare Triebenfeld from execution. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-051.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kontop to the Prince. The iron has not arrived, but the Execution has been lifted, so he leaves for Königsberg tomorrow. He will wait until he is back to judge the inheritance matter. There is a new decree on seizures (Arrestschlag) in Poland. He has summoned Honrichs, who promises the Prince several thousand. He calls Hawich a Cujon who keeps back original papers entrusted to him. Bethney is ill in Mal[z?]dorff. War rumours come from bankers in Züllichau. Postscript: Honrichs is coming and will bring money. Lines 14 to 17 are partly garbled. The letter does not touch Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-052.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Königsberg to the Prince. He handed the Prince's letter and its enclosures to the Queen, who received them with pleasure. She passed the matter to the Groß Kanzler, who handed it on to Cabinets und Cammergerichts Rath Allbrecht, and Triebenfeld now works on it with him. Beyme seems to insist on form, so the matter may drag on. Allbrecht is praised. The King has ordered, at the parole, that no one discuss politics, above all the war between France and Austria, because the reports contradict each other. Triebenfeld cannot yet say how long he will stay. Köckritz sends his compliments. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-053.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Königsberg to the Prince, answering his letters of the 24th and 29th of last month. The inheritance matter is still unresolved and lies with Beyme, together with Albrecht's opinion. The Auspfändung affair will go as the Prince wishes. On the Prince's military case, Triebenfeld urges him to write openly to the King; he praises Major von Pirch, and Köckritz is well-meaning. Massenbach's case depends on Scharnhorst, who is ill. The letter closes with war news: Austrian losses, Russia breaking off talks with Austria, and Schill's raid. Nothing concerns Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-054.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Glogau to the Prince. The Ober Post Amt held back the 100 Fr. d'or until he had paid postage and 480 rt, so the Prince's letter of 3 Feb arrived late. He begs for the iron to be at Boyadel by 23 April. Van der Lahr offers 5 1/2 rthl per Centner and should accept 6 rt. Triebenfeld means to obtain the 4000 rt assigned in Zagorowo. oe1bu9454-055.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Breslau after coming back from Glatz. Van der Lahr is now pursuing him in Breslau too, and he is waiting for 1000 Centner of iron to reach Kontop. The main subject is the Colonna inheritance in favour of the Queen: Götzen is a witness to the will; the Prussian Landrecht on codicils is quoted; the anonymous letter came from Gräfin Henckel. Götzen advises caution because of Graf Wratislaw. Triebenfeld proposes that the Queen take the estates worth 3 million, and he has drafted a letter from Götzen to her. He will then go to Königsberg. Also politics (war, contribution, Rüchel rumour, Massow's resignation) and, in the postscript, Bethusy's debts. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-057.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Świniary (Schweinern) after coming back from Königsberg. He is out of money: he was robbed on the road and has distraint (Execution) in his house. Money matters: the iron meant for Lahr is still lying at Konotop, he owes von der Lahr 3000 rt, and he borrowed money for the journey. From Königsberg: the King ordered that the Prince be spared, the inheritance matter is being handled through Hoyok in Warsaw and possibly Danckelmann, and the Prince is to be made General Gouverneur of Silesia. Also mentioned: Scharnhorst and Massenbach, Pirch, Erzherzog Ferdinand and Falkenhausen, the Tugendbund, and his son arrested at Kalisz. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-058.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Breslau. He has received the Prince's letter and 50 fr d'or through Bally, and the money has bought him 4 weeks' relief from execution. He is leaving for Kontop and Kosten, where he must provide Honrichs with armed men, and will then go to Schlawenschitz. He reports on Polish export rules and has written to the King urging a matching ban. He went to Kalisz himself to gather intelligence on the Poles' plans (restoring Poland, Konstantin as king). Garczynski and Zychlinski are his men but cannot act at present. He asks for news from Böhmen, will come in person within 10 days, and urges the Prince to heed his earlier advice on the military matter. Nothing is said about Trąbczyn specifically.

claims.statement: Dank für 50 fr d'or, erhalten durch Bally, damit für 4 Wochen von der Execution losgekauft

oe1bu9454-059.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kontop to the Prince about his own ruin. Kontop is under sequestration and there is execution on the Schweinern estates for 2560 rt interest and the van der Lahr debt. He has sent iron and boards to van der Lahr and still owes him money. His produce cannot be sold, which he blames on Königsberg letting the Poles import. He cannot come to the Prince. On the Prince's own affairs he says the Prince should write to the King; his friends are v. Pirch and Hache, and Gneisenau is not to be trusted. He adds political rumours, and says Honrichs may not take money out: it goes to Brzechffa in Kalisz, and Triebenfeld has asked whether cattle and grain could go instead. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-060.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Konotop in despair. He asks the Prince to raise 1800 rt and send it to Professor Schade. He says he cannot come as Lombardini's letter asks. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-063.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince. He has been ill for 7 weeks and is now recovering. He has a tenant for Konotop but must first pay 8000 rt of arrears. A man grown rich on French deliveries wants to buy wood. He hopes to be in Schlawenschitz by New Year. Affairs in Königsberg are said to be going well. Honrichs has arrived and brings a pro memoria with three points: deal with the Prefect who wants to buy the estates, because he could help recover the Trąbczyn estates; wrest from Dąbska the estates she seized; after the sequestration is lifted, the money must go to the Prince and the administrator must be rejected. Triebenfeld gave Honrichs provisional power of attorney and asks for authorisation. Hecker and Hawich stirred up Niedźwiecki, Ostarszewski and Lenski to denounce Honrichs, who was arrested. The denouncers have since retracted in writing.

oe1bu9454-064.notes: Three parts. (1) A short note from Triebenfeld to the Prince, dated 6 Xbr 1809. A Berlin friend reports the Queen's death at Strelitz and the King's illness. The Colonna matter is void, and the Prince should secure his 100000 rt. Triebenfeld wants to go to Berlin and is threatened with sequestration over interest on the Invaliden Capital. (2) A copy of Triebenfeld's letter to a friend (Weigelt) with a plan: Knobelsdorff's Bischdorf and Molna estates (700000 rt) in exchange for the Zagórów estates and quittance of the Weigelt (190000) and Stössel (180000) claims. (3) A Nachtrag of 30 October from Vienna: the Staats Kanzler supports the Prince's cause (112000 rt), and Triebenfeld begs for 300 rt in gold. Letters are to go via Ober Post Director Mann in Wien.

He plans an iron-for-spirits trade and asks the Koszęcin works to give him 300 Centner of iron on credit against an enclosed bill, delivered to Boyadel with the freight settled there. He recounts his debts. He reports a rumour that the Prince's case has been decided and that the Prince has been named General Gouverneur of Schlesien. Postscript: news about Sacken. oe1bu9454-066.notes: Triebenfeld, writing from Kontop, to the Prince. This is the continuation of doc. 63 on the Polish affairs. Expected verdict: the false denunciators get 6 years' fortress, the instigators are expelled. Hecker: Honrichs has a claim against him three times his paper caution. Colonists and old peasants begging for remission of interest should be refused; arrears count at a sale. Three bucks to be shot for Garczynski, Zakrzewski and Brzechffa. If things go well Honrichs gets the Casse back at New Year and the administration ends. Political rumours (King, Paris, Napoleon ill, Poles ordered back to Galicia). Postscript: iron held by the boatmen Kulawy and Neumann over freight; he asks for the receipts. Lawsuit costs (Trąbczyn, Niedźwiecki, Ostarszewski). Proposes delivery of 2000 Centner of rail iron for 8000 rt, with Coste paying.

oe1bu9454-067.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kontop to the Prince. He cannot leave because Coste has not come. Kontop is leased, Schweinern is not. On the Polish affair: Hawich accuses Honrichs of fraud. T. has summoned both and will send an actuary to Zagórów to find out who took money from the subjects and tenants. The sequestration was lifted by decree and only an overseer remains. More than 12 community deputations asked for time to pay. Hawich, Honrichs and Hecker took Hufen unlawfully. Berlin news comes via Grevenitz: Köckritz, Kleist, the general moratorium. He asks for the freight, toll and weigh slips for the iron. Postscript: Honrichs's letter came by express. T. suspects Hawich and Hecker, will hear from Brzechffa/Garczynski, and Hecker's paper caution is forfeit.

oe1bu9454-068.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kontop to the Prince. Honrichs has arrived and shown that Hawich's statements are false. oe1bu9454-071.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Kontop. The Rochlitz matter has been started in court (enclosure). Triebenfeld calls it a fraud, says he dismissed Rochlitz in 1804 as Generalbevollmächtigter and names Glenck as a witness. He asks for 2-3 signed and sealed blank printed Prozessvollmachten so that Melzig can pursue the case and collect outstanding arrears of about 18000 rt. He expects Honrichs tomorrow or the day after and will then come to Schlawenschitz. The postscript about the "Pohlinische Sachen" is fragmentary. Nothing in the letter concerns Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-072.notes: This is an unsigned letter to a "Krieges und Forst Rath", written by the owner of the Zagórów and Trąbczyn claims. He waited for the addressee to arrive with Brzechffa, and on the addressee's wish he dropped the exchange with General v Schimmelpfennig. He now assumes the lease to Brzechffa has fallen through. Pressed by his creditors, he has allowed a newly offered exchange partner to inspect the Zagórów estates. He also wants to sell his Praetensionen on the Trąbczyn estates, and sends a courier because of the original deed of gift. He asks whether Brzechffa's intercession in Warsaw over the Trąbczyn lawsuit has worked, and he asks for the 300 rt for Lieutenant Sommer. Several passages are garbled and the closing formula is corrupt.

claims.statement: Er hat das Tauschprojekt mit General v Schimmelpfennig aufgegeben.
Er vermutet, dass die Verpachtung an Brzechffa gescheitert ist.
Von Gläubigern bedrängt, hat er die Besichtigung der Güter um Zagórów für ein neues Tauschprojekt erlaubt.
claims.why: Lines 20-26 support the permission to inspect the Zagorower Güter for a new exchange project. But the reasons given there are his conjectures and the need to decide about his Polish estates. Lines 46-48 say he is pressed 'von allen Seiten' to carry out the arrangement with his creditors, not that the creditors are pressing him.

oe1bu9454-072a.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kopojno to the Prince. The lease of the Zagórów estates to Podprefect Brzechffa has been concluded. The joint trip to Schlawenschitz is postponed because Brzechffa and Prefect Garczynski were called to Warsaw; they will now leave after 11/12 March, and Brzechffa will bring 2-3000 rt. The Prince won the case against the Wrąbczyn peasants at the Tribunal. The Olesnicer case is expected to be won too. The Trąbczyn case is to go before the Rada Stanu. Triebenfeld sets out a calculation: 80000 Rthl of debts, 40000 rt from the old Hauländer for the forest, and the Dąbska owing damages and 6 years of revenue, against estates worth 300000 rt. He also reports heavy levies.

Am Schluss: die junge Fürstin, geplante Reise, Nachschrift.

Wegen der abgehenden Gelegenheit schreibt er nur kurz.

doubtful_words.note: Probably 'Dein Freund und Bruder' (Polish 'przyiaciela'); not provable.

oe1bu9454-072e.notes: A short Polish note from Brzechffa to Triebenfeld, whom he calls "Kochany Bracie". Because of various business he cannot leave Warsaw before the 15th of the month. He has reliable information that the Trąbczyn matter stands well and will explain in person when he returns. He writes little because the messenger is leaving. The German copy (72d) matches the text. Line 10 "obiacnie" probably stands for "objaśnię" (explain), but I cannot prove it. "[k?]ony" is in brackets, so it is left alone.

claims.statement: Brzechffa kann wegen verschiedener Geschäfte erst am 15. des Monats aus Warszawa abreisen.
Nach zuverlässigen Nachrichten steht die Sache wegen Trąbczyn gut.
Näheres will er nach seiner Rückkehr berichten.
Er schreibt nur kurz, weil die Gelegenheit abgeht.

oe1bu9454-072f.notes: Triebenfeld, from Kopojno, sick with podagra, reports to the Prince: excessive delivery (grain, straw) imposed on the Zagórów estates; Ober Prefectur Kalisz refused his objection and refused execution against peasants for arrears; the estates were sequestrated again; he hurried here; Podprefect Brzechffa agreed to pay the deliveries from 2000 rt he meant to bring to Sławięcice, receipts to count as lease; the sequestor was recalled and put under observation. Billeting, fled subjects, no money. Courts idle until 1 June; peasants went to Warsaw cassation court; decisions awaited; garbled plan to come at Johanni with money. Postscript: Honrichs to be arrested for embezzling taxes. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Den Zagórówer Gütern wurde eine übermäßige Lieferung an Getreide und Stroh angekündigt
Die Ober Prefectur in Kalisz lehnte Execution bei den Bauern zur Beitreibung rückständiger Zinsen ab
Die Güter wurden wieder unter Sequestration genommen
Brzechffa war bereit, die Lieferungen aus 2000 Rthl zu berichtigen, die er nach Sławięcice mitbringen wollte
claims.why: Laut Zeilen 23-24 hatte der Podprefect die 2000 rt liegen und wollte sie nach Schlawenschitz mitbringen. Dass Brzechffa dieser Podprefect ist, steht nicht ausdrücklich im Brief. Belegt ist nur, dass Brzechffa sofort bereit war (Z. 27-28).

claims.statement: Der Sequestor wurde abgerufen
Triebenfeld liegt mit Podagra

oe1bu9454-073.notes: This is a copy of the Prince's reply of 27 January 1812 from Schlawenschitz to Triebenfeld (called Forstrath), answering his letter of 1 January. It was dictated after he talked it over with H v Weithausen and Bally. It sets the Prince's terms for Brzechffa's lease offer on the Zagorower Güter: rent paid half-yearly in advance, a cash deposit, protection against remission claims, the tenant to bear all charges, and a fixed payment if the estate is sold during the lease. It reports that the Schimmelpfennig exchange has stalled and that he doubts the Weigelt/Stössel sale plan. It blesses the work on the Oleschnicer and Trąbczyner matter and mentions game and a dog. The passage on the 300 rt is garbled.

claims.statement: Bedingungen zum Pachtangebot Brzechffas: halbjährige Zahlung prenumerando, bare Caution, Schutz vor Remissions- und Regressklagen, Lasten beim Pächter, Abstandsquantum bei Verkauf
Triebenfeld soll bald mit Brzechffa kommen, Brzechffa soll mehrere tausend Rthl mitbringen
Güterhandel mit Schimmelpfennig nicht vorangekommen
Verkaufsprojekt an Weigelt und Stössel wenig aussichtsreich
Segenswunsch für die Oleschnicer und Trąbczyner Sache, Hoffnung auf bedeutende Summe

oe1bu9454-074a.notes: Copy of a fiscal application for arrest ("Pro Fisco", signed Seelmann, the sender is given as not identified) to the Kammergericht in Berlin on behalf of the General Invaliden Casse. Triebenfeld borrowed 50000 rt in 1805 and pledged the Prince's obligation of 250000 rt, secured on the Zagórów estates. Interest of 9375 rt has been unpaid since Nov 1807. The Kalisz prefecture has added the mortgage to the Bayonne sums, and Konotop and Świniary are heavily indebted. The application asks for arrest on the 80000 rt legacy from the Fürstin von Sacken's estate, reportedly due to the Prince and to be paid on to Triebenfeld. Kircheisen is the executor. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Arrestgesuch der General Invaliden Casse an das Kammergericht
Darlehn von 50000 Rthl an v. Triebenfeld, gesichert durch Obligation des Fürsten über 250000 Rthl auf die Zagórówer Güter

Arrest auf 80000 Rthl Vermächtnis der Fürstin von Sacken, Kircheisen als Testamentsvollstrecker
claims.why: Lines 78-80: the Casse has only heard that Kircheisen 'Executor ... sein soll'. This is hearsay, not fact.

doubtful_words.note: likely misreading of 'von Sacken' (cf. line 80 Fürstin von Sacken)

oe1bu9454-074b.notes: A short memo (P. M.) from Triebenfeld to the Prince. Zagórów needs an Ober Förster. Triebenfeld had lined up the old Richter's son for one post and the Nageln's nephew as Propinations Beamter. Because the Nageln has called her nephew away, Richter now has to run the propination. If the Prince wants to help Radszewski, he should send him quickly: 300 Rthl a year. Triebenfeld also asks for the Prince's opinion on the exchange of estates. There is a gap in line 3 ("bey der Bra[...]"), so it is unclear which post the son was meant for.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld hält die Anstellung eines Oberförsters in Zagórów für nötig.
Der Richter muss jetzt die Propination verwalten, weil die Nageln ihren als Propinationsbeamten vorgesehenen Neffen abgerufen hat.
Will der Fürst Radszewski helfen, soll er ihn schnell schicken; mit 300 Rthl jährlich muss dieser zufrieden sein.
Bittet um die Meinung des Fürsten zum Tausch der Güter.

oe1bu9454-074c.notes: Copied court papers. Part 1 (lines 1-19): order from the Königl. Preuß. Kammergericht, Berlin, 1 August 1811, to Minister von Kircheisen as executor of the will of the late Fürstin von Sacken. The same order went to Ober Medicinal Rath Cosmar and to Triebenfeld at Kontop. It says: if the General Invaliden Casse is right that the Prince's legacy of 80000 rt has been assigned to Triebenfeld, pay Triebenfeld nothing of it. Part 2 (lines 20-27): cover note from the Ober Landes Gericht von Schlesien in Glogau, 6 August, signed Fülleborn. It forwards the Kammergericht's summons to Triebenfeld and asks him to confirm receipt.

claims.statement: Das Kammergericht fordert Kircheisen als Testamentsvollstrecker der verstorbenen Fürstin von Sacken auf, Triebenfeld nichts auszuzahlen.

Dies gilt, falls die Klage der General Invaliden Casse zutrifft, wonach Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen ein Legat von 80000 Rthl erhalte und dieses Triebenfeld zur Begleichung seiner Forderungen angewiesen habe.
Gleichlautend an Cosmar und Triebenfeld.
claims.why: 'in simili' (lines 15-17) covers only Cosmar. The address to Triebenfeld (lines 18-19) is the heading of the separate Glogau letter from the Ober Landes Gericht, not a second copy of the Kammergericht letter.

claims.statement: Das Ober Landes Gericht von Schlesien übersendet Triebenfeld in Konotop die Vorladung und verlangt eine Empfangsbescheinigung.

oe1bu9454-074d.notes: Summons from the Königl. Preuß. Cammergericht in Berlin (signed Woldermann, with the name Stoewersand at the foot) to Triebenfeld at Konotop. The General Invaliden Casse asked for an arrest on the 80000 rt legacy that the late Fürstin von Sacken left to the Prince. The court granted the arrest and set a hearing for 23 August at 10 before Kammergerichtsrath Roitsch. Triebenfeld must appear in person or through a Justizkommissar, answer, state his damage and the amount of caution, and try for a settlement. If he does not appear, the arrest stands. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Die General Invaliden Casse hat gegen Triebenfeld einen Arrest auf das Legat von 80000 Rthl beantragt, das die verstorbene Fürstin von Sacken dem Fürsten von Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen vermacht hat.
Das Gericht hat den Arrest verhängt und einen Termin am 23. August um 10 Uhr vor Kammergerichtsrath Roitsch angesetzt.
Triebenfeld soll selbst oder durch einen Justizkommissar erscheinen, seine Einwendungen und seinen Schaden vortragen und die Höhe der Caution angeben.
Er soll mit dem Kläger einen Vergleich versuchen.
Bleibt er aus, bleibt der Arrest bestehen.
Es handelt sich um eine Vorladung des Kammergerichts Berlin.

doubtful_words.note: Garbled. Probably 'überhaupt aber über das, was' or something similar; not certain.

oe1bu9454-075.notes: Triebenfeld in Breslau writes to the Prince. He returns the letters of a "Gr. v. S." that the Prince had passed to him. He regrets losing the chance to gain the Prince 40 bis 50/m Rthl. Reinhardt writes from Bonn: nothing yet on the Assistenz des Fisci. Goldbeck reports a Berlin rumour that Hoym keeps the Südpreußisches Departement. Priebich, a confidant of Haugwitz, told Rath Kruger that Haugwitz will become minister. Chełmski has not appealed, so the estates may be leased at Johanni. Melzer was away when the express came back with news from Gravenitz; the form for the power of attorney will follow. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld schickt die mitgeteilten Schreiben des Gr. v. S. zurück

oe1bu9454-076.notes: A short note from Triebenfeld in Breslau to the Prince. He says a certain exchange of estates is under way and may soon be settled. He will travel to Berlin at the beginning of September and stay until the end of the month. There he hopes to see the Prince and report in person on several matters of business. Trąbczyn is not mentioned. In line 7, "dörfen" looks odd; it may be "dorten". Line 11 repeats "den, den".

claims.statement: Der Gütertausch ist im Gange und vielleicht bald abgeschlossen.
Er will Anfang September nach Berlin reisen und bis Ende des Monats bleiben.
Er hofft den Fürsten in Berlin wiederzusehen und persönlich über mehrere Geschäfte zu berichten.

Possibly a repeated word, or a misreading of "dann".

oe1bu9454-077.notes: Triebenfeld in Berlin reports to the Prince on a pending matter at court: a letter from the King sent via Geh. Rath Beyme, and the matter referred to Minister v Voss for a quick report. Glenck is to prepare the Anschläge so they match the Designation and the contracts. He has engaged a man in Potsdam, says Michaelis will ask for a Vollmacht, is arranging a loan, and asks for signed blank sheets (blanquets). He will visit Fürstin Sacken. Postscript on appointments: Buerensprung made Land Forstmeister, Wedel stays in post, Lindenau made Excellenz. The letter does not mention Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Die Sache läuft nach Wunsch, Schreiben des Königs über Beyme

Vollmacht für Michaelis erbeten

oe1bu9454-078.notes: Michaelis writes to the Prince from Berlin about the Prince's proposal, which has gone to Minister v. Voss. Michaelis called on Geh. Finanzrat Schulze, who knew nothing beyond having read the Prince's letter to Voss and took no position either way. Schulze suggested that Michaelis deposit a power of attorney in the Registratur. Triebenfeld told Michaelis that the cabinet orders are going to Voss now, so Schulze will have the royal order by Wednesday or Thursday. Michaelis proposes wording for the power of attorney (exchange of the granted estates for a Herrschaft at the Südpreußen Departement), asks for information and a receipt, and praises Triebenfeld's zeal. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-079.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince about the planned exchange of the Prince's granted estates (Güter Tausch, Krotoszyn affair). He is awaiting Minister von Voss's report. He reports that Schulenburg, Hoym (who offers 1000 rt) and Struensee support it, lists how the payoff sum is to be divided, and describes his informants in the Potsdam cabinet (200 fr d'or). Court politics on war and peace follow, with Hoym, Schulenburg and Struensee. Triebenfeld will stay in Berlin until the Krotoszyn matter is settled. He is negotiating 120/m Rthl from the Wittwen Casse on his own estates and asks for blanquets. PS: Fürstin Sacken, Haugwitz. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld wartet auf den Bericht des Ministers von Voss

oe1bu9454-080.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Berlin, a short follow-up to his letter of the previous day, which went with Hauptmann (u.?) Hahn. Hoym came back from Potsdam in good spirits; someone reports that the Prince was discussed there and that the King esteems him. There is talk in Berlin of marches or war, which Triebenfeld doubts because of the King's firm principles. Nothing has come back yet from Minister von Voss, and Triebenfeld hopes Voss will not act against the King's interest or the Prince's peace. The letter has nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld ergänzt sein Schreiben vom Vortag, das Hauptmann Hahn mitnahm.
Hoym kehrte zufrieden aus Potsdam zurück, wo nach Aussage eines anderen Mannes mehrfach vom Fürsten die Rede war.
Das bestätige, dass der König den Fürsten schätze; er hofft auf einen guten Ausgang.
In Berlin rede man von Märschen oder Krieg, er glaubt noch nicht daran.
Von Minister von Voss ist noch nichts zurück.
claims.why: Zeile 18 nennt nur 'des Herrn von Voss Excellenz'; dass er Minister ist, steht nicht im Brief.

doubtful_words.note: 'H. Hauptmann u. Hahn': may be 'v. Hahn', or two people may be meant.
The plural subject calls for 'haben'; this may be the writer's own slip.
The edition's formula is 'In tiefster Ehrfurcht ersterbe', but 'Verehrung' could be what the writer actually wrote.

oe1bu9454-081.notes: Michaelis writes from Berlin to the Prince. Triebenfeld and Eysenhardt are pressing him for news on the estate exchange (Gütertausch). Nothing has yet come in to the Südpreußische registry and expedition office, so the matter must still sit in the correspondence between Minister v. Voss and Geh. Finanzrat Schulze, and nothing has been decreed. He will not keep troubling Schulze with visits. He expects the Prince's power of attorney next Tuesday; with it he will prove his authority and get reliable information from Schulze. The letter is short and the text is sound, apart from small case errors and a few odd words.

claims.statement: Trotz Drängens von Triebenfeld und Eysenhardt kann er noch nichts Bestimmtes über den Gütertausch melden.
Bei der südpreußischen Expedition ist nichts eingegangen.
Die Sache steckt noch in der Korrespondenz zwischen v. Voss und dem Geheimen Finanzrat Schulze, und es ist noch nichts decretirt.
claims.why: Der Brief zieht das nur als Schluss daraus, dass nichts eingegangen ist ("dies ist ein Zeichen, daß ... stecken muß"). Die Behauptung stellt es als Tatsache hin. Die Zusammenfassung selbst gibt es mit "stecke also" schon als Schluss wieder.

claims.statement: Er erwartet die Vollmacht am kommenden Dienstag und will sich damit legitimieren und bei Schulze eine zuverlässige Erkundigung einholen.

oe1bu9454-082.notes: Eysenhardt senior writes from Berlin to Prince Hohenlohe. Minister v. Voss is still at Havelberg, so the King's Cabinets Schreiben in the Prince's matter was sent on to him there. Eysenhardt had a friend check the Kanzeley (chancery) and nothing has arrived yet. Voss may bring the letter himself, since he is returning 14 days early, next Thursday. If the letter is as decided as Triebenfeld says, Eysenhardt is sure all will go as wished, and his patrons have assured him of this. Second, Triebenfeld asked him for 300 Pr Courant for the Prince's use and on his account; Eysenhardt paid it against a receipt. A few words are garbled.

claims.statement: Das königliche Cabinets Schreiben wurde dem Minister v. Voss nach Havelberg nachgesandt.
In der Kanzeley ist es noch nicht eingegangen.
Voss kehrt vorzeitig am nächsten Donnerstag zurück und bringt es vielleicht selbst mit.
Lautet das Schreiben so entschieden wie von Triebenfeld dargestellt, erwartet Eysenhardt einen günstigen Ausgang.
Er hat v. Triebenfeld auf dessen Verlangen 300 Pr Courant für Rechnung des Fürsten gegen Schein gezahlt.

doubtful_words.note: possibly 'bereits' or 'bereit[s]'; the sense is unclear

oe1bu9454-083.notes: v. Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen about an exchange of estates. He reports that Krotoszyn is as good as granted, while Polajewo still meets hesitation; Geh. Finanz Rath Schulze has given assurances, and Polajewo could bring 100/m rt. He is worried that Prinz George will reach Breslau before him and asks the Prince to hold him there. Hoym has gone to Pommern, Voss returns Thursday, and Triebenfeld has written to Voss, Schulze, Beyme and the Oberst. The postscript carries court rumours: the King in a bad mood, Repnin under a ukase, Mencke active again, and a claim that the French want Hannover. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Krotoszyn wird dem Fürsten sicher gegeben
Bedenken wegen Polajewo, Schulze versichert, auch dies sei zu erhalten
bei Polajewo 100/m Rthl zu gewinnen, Hindernisse mit den Kammern
bittet, Prinz George aufzuhalten, bis er kommt
claims.why: Z. 25-26: Die Bitte ist bedingt ('Solte der Prinz ... eher als ich eintreffen'). Der Ort des Aufhaltens ist unklar (der entstellte Ausdruck 'in das Forte'). Dass der Prinz in Breslau aufgehalten werden soll, sagt der Brief nicht ausdrücklich.

claims.statement: Hoym nach Pommern gereist, Voss kommt Donnerstag zurück

oe1bu9454-084.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince about the exchange for Krotoszyn. The King has ordered Voss to settle it, and Voss asked for 4 weeks to submit the final report. The chambers are to check whether the revenues match. Because of the difficulties over Polajewo, Triebenfeld proposes lands from the Starostey Adelnau, which adjoins Krotoszyn, to make up the higher value. He is leaving for Betsche (Pszczew) to deal with Broniewski, and Prinz George will be in Breslau. Everyone except Voss is well disposed; Voss is governed by Kr Rath Nöldichen. Russian gossip follows (new mistress, Repnin reportedly arrested, the Empress confined). He expects to see the Prince in 5 days. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Königl. Majestät hat Voss mit der Regelung der Krotoszyn-Sache beauftragt; Voss erbat 4 Wochen für den Finalbericht
Die Kammern sollen prüfen, ob die Revenuen gleichkommen

oe1bu9454-085.notes: This is a copy of a letter from King Friedrich Wilhelm III to the Prince, sent from Berlin on 4 Dec 1798. The Prince had proposed exchanging his South Prussian estates for the domain offices of Krotoszyn and Polajewo. The King turns this down, relying on a report by Minister v. Voss. That report says Krotoszyn alone yields 49043 Rthl and that Triebenfeld received 26,000 Rthl compensation (Abstand) for giving up the lease in 1795. On that basis the state would lose 17400 Rthl a year. The Prince's estates were valued at 8650 Rthl and, after about 26,000 Rthl of improvements, now yield 40,500 Rthl. On 19 July Voss had already been told to reject such proposals. Several phrases are garbled.

claims.statement: Der König lehnt den Tausch der südpreußischen Güter gegen die Domänenämter Krotoszyn und Polajewo ab
Laut Bericht des Ministers v. Voss bringt Krotoszyn allein schon 49043 Rthl Revenue
claims.why: Laut Z. 10-12 gilt der Betrag nur, wenn die bei der jetzigen Verpachtung nicht veranschlagten Pertinenzien hinzukommen. Er ist also bedingt und kein gegenwärtiger Ertrag.

claims.statement: v. Triebenfeld erhielt für die Abtretung der Pacht einen Abstand von 26,000 Rthl
Der Staat verlöre jährlich 17400 Rthl
Die auf 8650 Rthl veranschlagten Güter des Fürsten bringen nach etwa 26,000 Rthl Meliorationen jetzt 40,500 Rthl
Voss wurde am 19. Juli angewiesen, solche Anträge abzuweisen

oe1bu9454-086.notes: Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen writes from Breslau to the King, answering the royal letter of 4 Dec 1798 that turned down the exchange of his South Prussian estates for the domain of Krotoszyn. He objects to Minister von Voss's report: Voss left out that the Prince had dropped Polajewo from the request, and he relied only on Kriegesrath Nöldichen. The Prince disputes the 49043 r yield Voss gives for Krotoszyn and the claimed loss of 17400 rt. He asks for an impartial commissioner to compare the two sets of estates, and says his aim was to raise capital to pay his debts. Trąbczyn is not mentioned.

claims.statement: Der Fürst widerspricht dem Bericht des Staatsministers von Voss zum Tausch seiner südpreußischen Güter gegen Krotoszyn.
Voss habe den Verzicht auf Polajewo nicht angezeigt.
claims.why: Zeilen 19-22 sind vorsichtig formuliert: 'wenn der Minister diese Modification ... nicht angezeigt haben sollte, wie ... zu erhellen scheint'. Das ist eine Vermutung und keine Feststellung. 'Verschwiegen' unterstellt zudem eine Absicht.

claims.statement: Der Bericht stütze sich nur auf Angaben des Kriegesrath Nöldichen.

Krotoszyn zahlt 30100 Rthl Pacht, die Güter des Fürsten tragen 41500 Rthl.

unclear, perhaps 'berichtet' or 'gerichtet'; the same word appears in doc 87

oe1bu9454-087.notes: Fürst Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen schreibt an Obrist von Köckritz über den gescheiterten Tausch seiner vom König verliehenen südpreußischen Güter gegen die Krotoszyner Güter. oe1bu9454-103.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Breslau about several lawsuits. In the Broniewski case he is holding off a settlement because of the coming court date, Rapacki's proofs, and the planned Krotoszyn exchange. He also covers Schlabrendorff's bill of exchange, the Chełmski lawsuit won on appeal, and the Brzyze and Winicer forest disputes. Most of the letter answers the Minister's claim that the Prince received too many estates. The confiscated Prusimski estates count as bought, not given. He lists yields: Kaemen/Kulm 6000, Trąbczyn 8400, Szetlewek 1600, Brzyze 4000 Rthl. The gifted church estates have 8640 Rthl in revenues plus a surplus of about 14000. He compares these with other grants, and Glenck is to pass this account to Prittwitz.

oe1bu9454-106.notes: Triebenfeld, writing from Berlin, answers the Prince's letter about an estate purchase that the Jew Dann proposed. Hof Fiscal Michaelis passed that letter on. Dann hopes to talk H. v. Echart, the buyer of the Lichtenau houses, into it, and Triebenfeld dismisses the plan as a swindle. Bad news follows: a contumacial decree of the Posen government would take the Brzyzer Güter back. The Cammern are intriguing over the forests, lawsuits and costs are mounting, and the exchange (Tausch) is stalled because the ministers act as sovereigns. In the postscript he mentions P's ill will and the Prince's fall from his horse, which Eysenhardt reported. Nothing about Trąbczyn.
