Die Cammern intrigieren wegen der Forsten, Prozesse verursachen hohe Kosten.
Die Tauschsache stockt; die Minister würden den Tausch nur auf Befehl des Monarchen zulassen.
claims.why: Dass die Sache stockt, steht in Z. 34-36. Die Aussage über die Minister ist aber nur Triebenfelds Vermutung ('so glaube ich', Z. 37).

claims.statement: Er bittet den Fürsten nach dessen Sturz vom Pferd um Vorsicht.
claims.why: Den Sturz kennt Triebenfeld nur vom Hörensagen ('wie nur Eysenhardt sagt', Z. 53). Er ist also berichtet und nicht als Tatsache belegt.

doubtful_words.note: name uncertain; possibly Eckart or Echaust
subject 'die Cammern' plural; possibly 'machen' or singular 'Cammer'

oe1bu9454-107.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince about the separation affair with the Fürstin Sacken. He forwards a letter from Obrist von Zastrow, holds a royal cabinet letter until the Prince arrives, was not received by the Fürstin, sends her a Zastrow letter to Köckritz. Her declaration (via 'Hein', garbled): she will never return, wants to live freely on 2/m rt appanage, left out of aversion and to protect her children's fortune. Her circle: Rietesel, Cosmar, Heinitz, Hoym, Selle. Friends urge firmness. Court rumour: Suvarow beaten and captured. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Leitet Schreiben des Obristen von Zastrow weiter
Behält das Cabinets Schreiben bis zur Ankunft des Fürsten
Von der Fürstin Sacken nicht empfangen; Schreiben des Fürsten übergeben lassen
Fürstin will nie zurück, frei leben, mit 2/m Rthl Appanage zufrieden
claims.why: Zeile 33 ist verstümmelt, gibt die Erklärung aber offenbar aus zweiter Hand wieder ('durch Hein[itz?] ... habe erklärt'). Die Zusammenfassung macht aus dieser Hörensagen-Angabe eine Tatsache.

claims.statement: Gründe: Abneigung, Liebe zu den Kindern
Freunde wünschen Festigkeit gegenüber der Fürstin Sacken
Nachricht am Hof: Suvarow geschlagen und gefangen

oe1bu9454-108.notes: Triebenfeld to the Prince, Breslau 22 July 1800, in distress over Prinz George: no reply or remittances despite letters delivered via Präsident v. Schuckman; Jew Kuh sued for 5800 Rthl with execution decree, arrest threatened Friday; minister (visited at Dyhrenfurth) to calm him, delayed to Thursday. Accounting: the Prince has encumbered the estates with 270000 Rthl, sold to him for 280000, rest 10000. Due: Liepman Meyer 20000, 12000 on 7 August; total 37800. Wants to go seek the Prince; asks for a way out. Not about Trąbczyn explicitly.

claims.statement: Prinz George antwortet trotz zugestellter Briefe (Schuckmann) nicht, schickt keine Remessen
Kuh verklagte ihn wegen 5800 Rthl, Exekutionsdekret, Freitag zahlen oder Arrest
Minister wollte Kuh beruhigen, kommt erst Donnerstag
claims.why: Lines 12-14: The minister promised to calm the Jew. That he will only come on Thursday is hearsay ('da heißt es'), not a fact.

claims.statement: Güter mit 270000 Rthl verschuldet, für 280000 Rthl verkauft
Liepman Meyer 20000 Rthl, 7. August 12000 Rthl, zusammen 37800 Rthl
claims.why: 20000 + 12000 is not 37800. The 'Post von 37800 rt' in line 32 also includes Kuh's 5800 Rthl (line 29), so the total is attached to the wrong items.

claims.statement: will den Prinzen aufsuchen, bittet um Ausweg

oe1bu9454-109.notes: Private note to a "Lieber Freund", signed v Triebenfeld, but the metadata gives the sender as not identified, so the summary uses "der Schreiber". Wildegansch is in Berlin and claims the Fürst sent him. The writer says Wildegansch and his followers made up a money deal with Asch and Schlabrendorff to cheat the Fürst over the costs, and that nothing will be decided for 2 months. Postscript: Bukowiecki offers only 2400 rt a year to lease Betsche (Pszczew). A Jew, Aich (probably Asch), and Schlabrendorff's front man mean to sue the writer over a bill of exchange of 11/m given to Schlabrendorff and to obtain an execution decree. The friend is asked to warn Seiner Durchlaucht. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Wildegansch ist in Berlin und behauptet, der Fürst habe ihn gesandt
Er erfand mit seinem Anhang ein Geldgeschäft mit Asch und Schlabrendorff, um den Fürsten um die Kosten zu prellen
In 2 Monaten wird nichts entschieden
claims.why: Z. 22-23 geben das nur als Gehörtes wieder: 'Wie ich aber höhre, so wird im 2 Monats ... nichts entschieden werden'.

claims.statement: Bukowiecki will für Pszczew nur 2400 Rthl Jahrespacht zahlen
Man will den Schreiber wegen eines an Schlabrendorff gegebenen Wechsels von 11/m verklagen und ein Exekutionsdekret erwirken
claims.why: Z. 35 leitet das als Gehörtes ein: 'Hier höhre ich auch daß ...'. In der Zusammenfassung fehlt dieser Vorbehalt.

claims.statement: Der Freund soll den Fürsten warnen

doubtful_words.note: the next letter has 'Wildegansct'; settled form uncertain

oe1bu9454-110.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. He reports that he has settled the business of the documents (Urkunden) for all the ecclesiastical estates. The fee first demanded was 2½ times that for the first document, because of the value stated in the first ministerial report. He now pays only 240 Fr d'or and about 200 rt, borrowed from Geheimer Ober Rechnungsrath Mathias, who needs it back in 14 days. He asks the Prince to assign the money quickly. He himself will get no money before Johanni. He expects news tomorrow in the Prince's other matter. The NB on line 23 is unclear. Nothing concerns Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld meldet, er habe das Geschäft wegen der Urkunden über sämtliche geistliche Güter abgeschlossen.
claims.why: Der Brief sagt 'glaube ich ... abgemacht zu haben'. Triebenfeld glaubt also nur, das Geschäft erledigt zu haben. Die Zusammenfassung stellt es als Tatsache dar.

claims.statement: Sollte sich sein Aufenthalt hinziehen, will er sie mit der nächsten Post nach Wrocław schicken.
Anfangs verlangte man das 2½-fache, jetzt zahlt er nur 240 Fr d'or und etwa 200 Rthl.
Das Geld hat er beim Geheimen Ober Rechnungsrath Mathias geliehen, der es in 14 Tagen zurück braucht.
Er bittet den Fürsten, es bald anzuweisen.
In der anderen Sache des Fürsten hofft er morgen mehr zu erfahren.

doubtful_words.note: The postscript's meaning and its figures are unclear; left out of the summary.

oe1bu9454-111.notes: Triebenfeld in Berlin to the Prince. He cannot raise the money to redeem the Urkunde (compare doc. 110: 240 Fr d'or and about 200 rt for the documents on the church estates). He blames Wildegans for ruining his credit, has paid 300 Rtrl as a deposit to the friend who arranged the matter, and asks for an Anweisung. He calls Köckritz and Zastrow true friends, but because of the gossip he will keep his distance. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld kann das Geld zur Auslösung der Urkunde nicht aufbringen, da Wildegansct ihm allen Kredit verderbe.
Dem Freund, der die Sache gemacht hat, gab er 300 Rthl als Angeld aus seinem Reisegeld.
Er bittet um eine Anweisung auf die 240 f. d'or und 200 Rthl Courant, sonst drohe ein böser Streich.
claims.why: Im Brief steht 'auf die 240 f. d'or um 200 Rt Courant'. Das ist ein einziger Betrag mit Umrechnungsangabe. Das 'und' macht daraus zwei getrennte Summen.

claims.statement: Köckritz und Zastrow seien wahre Freunde des Fürsten.
Wegen des Geklätsches will er sich im Hintergrund halten.

doubtful_words.note: Doc. 109 has 'Wildegansch'. The final 'ct' may be a misreading of 'ch', but a single witness in another letter does not prove it.
Elsewhere the formula is 'In tiefster Submission'. This may be a misreading, but the writer's wording varies, so it is not proven.

oe1bu9454-112.notes: This is a postscript by Triebenfeld to a letter he had already sealed. Hoffrath Wunster told him that Wildeganst and the Jew Heymann did nothing in the Prince's matter. Wildeganst also said that judgment had been given on the bill of exchange for 11/m Rthl that Triebenfeld signed for the Prince, and that Triebenfeld is to be arrested. The Amtpfänder Rudolph has asked for him at his house. He begs the Prince to make arrangements quickly. Prinz George sold Triebenfeld's estates for 750000 rt and bought tangled ones. Triebenfeld suggests the Prince move Graf Schlabrendorff to take the bill back from the Jews. Nothing about Trąbczyn. Lines 28 and 44 are garbled.

claims.statement: Hoffrath Wunster berichtet, dass Wildeganst und der Jude Heymann in der Sache des Fürsten nichts getan haben.
Nach Wildeganst ist über den Wechsel über 11/m Rthl bereits erkannt, Triebenfeld soll arretiert werden.
Der Amtpfänder Rudolph hat sich nach ihm erkundigt.
Er fleht um schleunige Vorkehrungen gegen die Verhaftung.
Prinz George hat seine Güter für 750000 Rthl verkauft.
Vorschlag, dass der Fürst Graf Schlabrendorff bewegen möge, den Wechsel von den Juden zurückzunehmen.

oe1bu9454-113.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince in distress. The Prince has assured him that the matter of the 11000 rt with Asch and Gad is settled. But an arrest order in the case still stands against him: he is to be arrested if the Prince does not pay the promised 4000 rt. Prinz George will not commit himself and keeps dragging out Triebenfeld's own affair. Wildeganst sends word that Asch and Gad would wait until Johanni, which Triebenfeld says does not save him. He begs the Prince to settle the matter with the 4000 rthl. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Dank für die Zusicherung, mit Asch und Gad sei wegen der 11000 Rthl alles abgemacht
Arrest gegen ihn; Verhaftung, falls die versprochenen 4000 Rthl nicht gezahlt werden
Prinz George erklärt sich über nichts und verschleppt seine Sache
Wildeganst lässt sagen, Asch und Gad würden bis Johanni warten; keine Rettung
claims.why: Zeile 24 hat 'der Asch und Geld'. Dass 'Geld' für Gad steht, ist eine Deutung eines verderbten Wortes. Sicher ist nur, dass Asch und jemand Weiteres (Plural 'würden') bis Johanni warten würden.

claims.statement: Bitte, die Sache durch die 4000 Rthl zu bereinigen

doubtful_words.note: probably 'mir' (die Gnade gehabt, mir zu versichern)
the usual closing formula is 'In tiefster Ehrfurcht ersterbe'; the word may be misread

oe1bu9454-114.notes: A short, badly garbled note to Krieges Rath von Triebenfeld. The sender is not identified ("Frig[?]") and signs as "unterthäniger Knecht". Someone unnamed (the name is missing at line 4) is called a scoundrel who made difficulties for Sr. Durchlaucht; now that nothing more can be squeezed out, he wants to conclude the whole matter. The writer hopes it will be settled soon so that Triebenfeld is no longer troubled, and there is a garbled mention of Schlabrendorff. On his own affair: it is neither good nor bad; "L. Asch" wants something (garbled) but will not succeed, and the writer expects a reply today. Things will be collected on Tuesday or at the latest Wednesday. His health is improving.

claims.statement: Ein Ungenannter wird als abgefeimter Bube bezeichnet, der Sr. Durchlaucht viele Schwierigkeiten gemacht habe
Da nichts mehr zu erpressen sei, wolle er das Ganze schließen
Der Schreiber hofft auf baldigen Abschluss, damit Triebenfeld nicht länger gekränkt werde
In seiner eigenen Sache wolle Asch etwas erreichen, was ihm nicht gelingen solle
claims.why: 'Der L. Asch jen will zullen' ist verstümmelt. Der Name 'Asch' und das 'erreichen' sind aus unleserlichen Wörtern gedeutet. Sicher lesbar ist nur, dass jemand etwas will, was ihm nicht gelingen soll.

claims.statement: Abholung am Dienstag, spätestens am Mittwoch
Seine Gesundheit bessere sich

doubtful_words.note: garbled; what is collected is unclear

oe1bu9454-115.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. He excuses himself from the midday meal because his tenant at Schweinern (Świniary) needs him: the peasants refuse their services. He reports a talk with the Minister about Schlabrendorff. The Minister is annoyed that the Prince tells him nothing. He has written to Schlabrendorff to be in Breslau on the 15th, to withdraw all complaints, and warned that he could not protect him. He has instructed Asch, who goes to "Stolze" (reading unclear) the day after tomorrow. Triebenfeld goes to Lądek tomorrow, will be back on the 15th and will bring in Hirsch. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Pächter in Świniary bittet dringend, die Bauern in Ordnung zu bringen, die die Dienste verweigern
entschuldigt Fernbleiben vom Mittag
Minister nimmt es krumm, dass der Fürst ihm nichts sagt
claims.why: Line 11 says 'so scheint er es etwas krum zu nehmen': this is Triebenfeld's impression, not a fact.

claims.statement: Minister bestellt Schlabrendorff zum 15., rät Rücknahme aller Klagen, könne ihn sonst nicht retten
Asch soll Schlabrendorff dazu bewegen, am 15. hier zu sein
Triebenfeld geht nach Lądek, am 15. zurück, will Hirsch hinzuziehen

oe1bu9454-116.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Breslau. He is ill and cannot come in person to take orders about the sale, or hereditary lease (Erbpacht), of the estates. The Poles keep choosing him as arbiter, but there is no fixed plan. He reports a rumour: Trąbczyn carries 150000 rt of debt, which Walichnowski would take over, and he is still supposed to pay 56000 rt plus a canon of 5000 rt a year. Triebenfeld calls this misunderstood gossip. He proposes firm terms for Walichnowski: 60000 or 80000 rt purchase money now and 4-5000 rt Erbzins a year for ever. He asks that the note be kept confidential and that the Prince send instructions secretly. Walichnowski is genuinely keen to acquire the Trąbczyn estates.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld ist krank und kann nicht persönlich Befehle zum Güterverkauf einholen.
Gerede: auf Trąbczyn hafteten 150000 Rthl Schulden, die Walichnowski übernehmen solle, und er solle dennoch 56000 Rthl und einen Canon von 5000 Rthl jährlich zahlen.
Er hält das für missverstandenes Gerede und fürchtet um die Ehre des Fürsten.
Vorschlag: Walichnowski soll 60000 oder 80000 Rthl Erbkaufgeld und 4 bis 5000 Rthl jährlichen Erbzins zahlen, als festes Wort.
Bittet, das Billet niemandem zu zeigen und ihm im Stillen Weisung zu geben.
Walichnowski will die Trąbczyner Güter wirklich erwerben.

oe1bu9454-117.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince about a Grotowski credit. Weigel, backed by Triebenfeld's guarantee, is to pay Grotowski 30/m rt plus interest. First Grotowski must execute a cession instrument in court, which Hoffrath Ebersbach has drafted, because the Banque will not discount before that. The Prince is asked to forward Weigel's letter to Grotowski by express. The letter also reports the deaths of Hauptmann v Müllern and of Morgenbeßer, gives news of Nelson and the mood in Vienna, and says Bernhardi has written to Stössel. In the postscript, Grotowski is to tell his Mandatarius in Kalisz to inform the Regierung that he is satisfied, so that there is no further talk of Subhastation, all before the 22nd. The estates are not mentioned.

claims.statement: Weigel sichert gegen Garantie Triebenfelds v. Grotowski 30/m Rthl samt Zinsen zu
Banque discontirt erst nach Cession; gerichtliches Cessions Instrument über 30/m Rthl nötig
Hoffrath Ebersbach hat das Instrument entworfen
Fürst soll Weigels Brief per Expressen an Grotowski schicken
Mandatarius in Kalisz soll der Regierung melden, dass keine Subhastation mehr anstehe
Tod des Hauptmanns v Müllern und Morgenbeßers
Nelsons Sieg über die Franzosen von Toulon, Jubel in Wien
Bernhardi hat an Stössel geschrieben

oe1bu9454-118a.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince about offers for the estates. Kunckel came with 2 colonists from Oleśnica who offer 1500 rt and want a contract. Triebenfeld doubts they can raise the 17000 Rthl due at Martini and Johanni and calls them fortune-seekers. He will only contract if the Prince orders it. Kunckel also holds a commission from Oberamtmann Nerlich, who wants Trąbczyn or Zagórów in Erbpacht and has 80000 rt in cash. Walichnowski wants to know what he should pay. Urbanowski has sent for the Trąbczyn Anschlag. Triebenfeld asks for instructions.

claims.statement: Kunckel und 2 Kolonisten aus Oleśnica bieten 1500 Rthl und wollen einen Vertrag.
Triebenfeld hält sie für Glücksritter, die die 17000 Rthl zu Martini und Johanni kaum zahlen könnten, und rechnet mit endlosen Prozessen.
Nur auf Befehl des Fürsten will er einen Vertrag entwerfen lassen.
Oberamtmann Nerlich will durch Kunckel Trąbczyn oder Zagórów in Erbpacht nehmen und hat 80000 Rthl bar.
Walichnowski fragt, was er zahlen soll.
Urbanowski hat den Trąbczyner Anschlag angefordert.
Triebenfeld bittet um Weisung.

doubtful_words.note: The sense requires 'den Contract', but this may be the writer's own den/dem confusion, so it is not corrected.
Probably 'dem' (Urbanowski), again possibly the writer's usage.
Probably 'trotz', broken across the line end.

oe1bu9454-118b.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince, a short note that survives in two copies (118b and 118c). Gräfin Schlabrendorff will wait for her 50000 Rthl until 1 January 1805. Homuth could not get a longer term from her. She complains of her loss because she gets no interest. If the Prince pays no interest until then, 2500 Rthl are gained. Homuth asks for the Vergleich so he can draft it and send it to her for execution, and he will try to recover the old bills of exchange. The Conducteur Cabanis has left and will hire a peasant cart for 4 or 5 Rthl outside town, because the coachmen in Breslau wanted 20 Rthl plus extras. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Gräfin Schlabrendorff will mit den 50000 Rthl bis 1. Januar 1805 warten; längere Frist konnte Homuth nicht erreichen
Sie beklagt Verlust, da sie keine Zinsen erhält
Ohne Zinszahlung bis dahin sind 2500 Rthl gewonnen
Homuth bittet um den Vergleich zur Vollziehung durch die Gräfin und will die alten Wechsel herausbekommen
claims.why: Zeilen 14-15: er will nur probieren, ob er die alten Wechsel herausbekommen kann.

claims.statement: Conducteur Cabanis abgereist; Mietkutscher verlangten 20 Rthl

doubtful_words.note: capital after 'und' (copy: 'um'); the transition at the line end is unclear

oe1bu9454-118c.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. Gräfin Schlabrendorff will wait for the 50000 Rthl until 1 January 1805. Homuth could not get her to agree to a longer term. If no interest is due before then, Triebenfeld advises accepting, since 2500 Rthl are gained. Homuth asks for the Vergleich so he can draft the deed for the countess, and he will try to get the old Wechsel back. The postscript says Conducteur Cabanis has left and will hire a peasant cart outside the city for 4 or 5 rt. Coachmen in Breslau wanted 20 rt. Nothing here on Trąbczyn. A parallel copy (118b) supports two corrections.

claims.statement: Gräfin Schlabrendorff will mit den 50000 Rthl bis zum 1. Januar 1805 warten, einen längeren Termin konnte Homuth nicht erreichen.
Sie beklagt ihren Verlust.
Muss der Fürst bis dahin keine Zinsen zahlen, rät Triebenfeld, den Termin anzunehmen, da 2500 Rthl gewonnen seien.
Homuth bittet um den Vergleich, um die Urkunde aufzusetzen, und will die alten Wechsel zurückbekommen.
claims.why: Lines 15-16: Homuth will only try to see whether he can get the old bills back ('wird probiren, ob er ... heraus bekommen kan').

claims.statement: Cabanis ist abgereist und will draußen eine Bauernfuhre für 4 oder 5 Rthl mieten.
claims.why: Lines 18-20: Cabanis only believes he can get the cart for 4 or 5 rt ('die er glaubt vor 4 oder 5 rt. zu erhalten').

claims.statement: Die Mietkutscher in Breslau verlangten 20 Rthl.

doubtful_words.note: Also 'Entter' in 118b. Possibly a misreading of 'Futter' (fodder), but this cannot be proven.
This heading line is missing from the copy 118b. It may have been added in the edition or come from a different part of the sheet.

oe1bu9454-119.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Breslau. Prinz Biron says Uminski finds the price too high but wants a letter to the administrator of the Kamionna estates so he can inspect them. Triebenfeld thinks Uminski is not serious, since Broniewski still holds the estates. The messenger from Zagórów has brought Glenck's table, which shows 31000 Morgen of demesne land that could be divided up. Triebenfeld proposes sending the surveyor Cabanis to recruit about 500 Hussite settlers. Three years ago Cabanis divided a small estate near Strehlen among such people. Rapacki's prospective buyers want long payment terms. Schöneich plans the same kind of sale. Trąbczyn is not mentioned.

claims.statement: Vorschlag, Cabanis zu den Husiten zu schicken und etwa 500 Wirte anzuwerben
Glencks Tabelle aus Zagórów: an 31000 Morgen Dominialgründe zu dismembrieren
Cabanis teilte bei Strehlen ein Gütchen an Husiten auf, die für 23 Hufen 25/m Rthl bar zahlten
Uminski findet laut Prinz Biron den Preis hoch, will die Kamionna-Güter aber besichtigen
Triebenfeld hält das für Spott, da Broniewski noch in den Gütern sitzt
Rapackis Kaufwillige verlangen weit aussehende Zahlungstermine

doubtful_words.note: probably 'erlauben' (before 'wird'); could also be the writer's own grammar
odd in this context; the meaning is doubtful
a small estate near Strehlen, not Pszczew (Betsche); do not identify it with Pszczew

oe1bu9454-120.notes: Triebenfeld to the Prince, Breslau. The surveyor Cabanis is back: Hussites in Husinich/Hussinitz and Rentsch want to buy land at 300 Rthl per Hufe plus 15 rt yearly Zins. They have sent an express to their Moravian brethren and plan to come in corpore within 14 days. Cabanis is to go back and spur them on through the local clergyman. Countess Schlabrendorff will not release the instrument until she has the other 50/m rt. Homuth has arranged a term to 1 Jan 1805. Kunckel is expected; his mother is destitute, and the Prince is asked for a few Thaler. The letter does not name the estate the land is for.

claims.statement: Cabanis meldet Kaufwillige unter den Husiten in Husinich und Rentsch
halten 300 Rthl pro Hufe und 15 Rthl Zins für billig
Boten an mährische Glaubensbrüder
claims.why: Zeile 7 nennt 'einen Expressen', also einen einzigen Boten, nicht mehrere.

claims.statement: wollen binnen 14 Tagen in Corpore erscheinen
Cabanis soll sie über den Geistlichen in Hussinitz antreiben
Schlabrendorff gibt Instrument erst nach Erhalt der übrigen 50/m Rthl heraus
Homuth bewirkt Frist bis 1. Januar 1805
Kunckel wird erwartet
bittet um ein paar Thaler für Kunckels notleidende Mutter

doubtful_words.note: probably a misreading of 'hinreisen' or similar
unclear; the continuation of 'Instru¬' is probably 'Instrument'
written 'Hussinitz' on line 14; the place name form is uncertain

oe1bu9454-122.notes: A short note, signed v Triebenfeld, written at Breslau on 6 April 1804. The sender and recipient are given as not identified, so the summary calls him "der Schreiber". He forwards a Billet that had been left at his old lodging. Herr Homuth asks for this Post to be settled quickly so that he can confirm receipt of 166 rt. 16 g. Cabanis is leaving by post for Hussinitz, and the writer expects a quick success there. This fits the previous letter, about the Hussites wanting to buy land. No news has come from Berlin or Frankfurth. The text is sound.

claims.statement: Der Schreiber leitet ein Billet weiter, das versehentlich im alten Logis liegen geblieben war.
Homuth bittet, die Post bald zu berichtigen, damit er den Eingang der 166 Rthl 16 g anzeigen kann.
Cabanis reist mit der Post nach Hussinitz ab; der Schreiber erwartet schnellen, glücklichen Erfolg.
Aus Berlin oder Frankfurth keine Nachricht.
claims.why: Lines 11-12 sagen nur, dass er 'heute' keine Sylbe erhalten hat. Ohne 'heute' klingt es, als sei nie eine Nachricht gekommen.

doubtful_words.note: Grammatically one would expect 'glücklichſten', but this may be the writer's own form or a machine misreading. Left unchanged.

oe1bu9454-123.notes: Triebenfeld sends on to the Prince a letter from Kunckel that came by Estaffette and asks for instructions. He advises settling with Otocki and says a friendly settlement at 1500 or 2000 rt would be good. He leaves it to the Prince whether Kunckel should get the power of attorney for the settlement. He fears that Kunckel and Jentsch are working against each other and advises instructing both of them. Glenck did not come back and left the Konotop accounts behind, which explain the whole matter. Nothing in the letter concerns Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld reicht ein per Estaffette eingegangenes Schreiben Kunckels ein und bittet um Verhaltungsbefehle.
Er hält ein Abkommen mit Otocki für nötig; ein gütlicher Vergleich, bei dem Otocki mit 1500 oder 2000 Rthl zufrieden wäre, sei vorteilhaft.
Ob Kunckel Vollmacht zum Vergleich erhalten soll, stellt er dem Fürsten anheim.
Er fürchtet, dass Kunckel und Jentsch gegeneinander handeln, und rät, beide zu instruieren.
Glenck kam nicht mehr, ließ aber die Rechnungen von Konotop zurück, die über alles Aufschluss geben.

doubtful_words.note: 'dabei lezt einreiche' reads oddly; perhaps a misreading of 'unterthänigst' or of a similar word.
'so wären es eine ... Sache' would need 'wäre'; this may be the writer's own slip.

oe1bu9454-124.notes: Triebenfeld writes a short note to the Prince from Wrocław. He encloses his draft reply to Kunckel for the Prince to check against his wishes. He asks that someone make fair copies of both letters, because his wife is being buried today and he has gone with the children to his brother-in-law's. He will explain everything in his own letter to Kunckel. The last sentence mentions a map of Kopojno, Skokum and Swiątniki and breaks off with "habe ich hier". There is nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Legt den Entwurf der Antwort an Kunckel zur Prüfung vor, ob sie dem Willen des Fürsten entspricht
Bittet, beide Schreiben von jemandem ins Reine schreiben zu lassen
Seine Frau wird heute beigesetzt, er hat sich mit den Kindern zum Schwager zurückgezogen

oe1bu9454-125.notes: Short note from Triebenfeld in Breslau to the Prince. The people from Oleśnica have arrived with the money and will call on the Prince at 4 o'clock. Triebenfeld has already negotiated something with them, will report on it in the afternoon, and thinks the Prince will not be displeased. Nothing about Trąbczyn. The writer's grammar is nonstandard throughout ("mit die Gelder", "mit sie"), so "im 4 Uhr" may be his own wording and is not corrected. "Euer Durchlaucht" is an acceptable form.

claims.statement: Die Leute aus Oleśnica sind mit den Geldern angekommen und wollen um 4 Uhr beim Fürsten erscheinen.
v. Triebenfeld hat mit ihnen verhandelt und will am Nachmittag darüber Vortrag halten.
Er glaubt, es werde dem Fürsten nicht unlieb sein.

doubtful_words.note: The sense requires 'um 4 Uhr'. This may be a misreading, but it may also be the writer's own nonstandard grammar, so it is not corrected.

oe1bu9454-126.notes: Short note from Triebenfeld in Breslau to the Prince. Cabanis has come back with the "Hussiten", who liked it very much. They want to hurry home, gather their fellow believers and settle everything within 14 days. Cabanis has news that has to be discussed, and someone must go there at once. Triebenfeld is negotiating with the people from Oleśnica (see doc. 125) and asks the Prince to call on him for a quarter of an hour after the parade, hear them himself and give orders. The irregular grammar is the writer's own (mit die, Seiner Hochfürstliche, den = denn). There is nothing to correct.

oe1bu9454-127.notes: Short note from Triebenfeld to the Prince (Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen), Breslau. An unnamed "Prinz" has not paid the interest, so Triebenfeld as guarantor must pay 910 rt (700 for the inventory, 175 in interest since 1799, 35 in court costs). His funds are exhausted after paying 1537 rt 12 gg yesterday in the "Nudnichische" matter (possibly Rudnicki, cf. doc. 128), which the Prinz had promised to settle. Wildegans and Heyman Pincus promise to settle everything. He asks the Prince to help with 900 rt, offers to support him with timber money at Johanni, and wants to avoid Execution. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-128.notes: Triebenfeld schreibt aus Trąbczyn an den Fürsten über die Missstände vor Ort: 11 Prozesse, für die er Prorogation erhalten hat, dazu Pächter, die hohe Abstandsgelder fordern. Rudnickis zu Johanni und die spätere Verpachtung. Der Landrath hilft beim Grundzins der alten Unterthanen (1 Rthl pro Hufe) und bei Käufern für 87 Hufen. Die 3 B. bieten an, den Olesnicer Contract aufzuheben. Glenck verspottet den Olesnicer Contract in einem Brief an den Landrath, will Kunckel entfernt sehen und bietet Geldgeschäfte an. oe1bu9454-129.notes: A short note from Triebenfeld in Breslau to the Prince. He has no letters from Berlin or Frankfurt and is anxious, and asks for any news from Glenck. On Kolzig, Amelang does not answer. If Amelang stays silent, the sale of Kontop (Konotop) must be pushed hard. He summoned the tenant Bernhardi and told him to recommend the estates to buyers, because a tenant might block the sale or be bribed. Bernhardi is to receive Ludolf and Stubenrauch well. In the afternoon he will bring out the things for Südpreußen. Nothing here concerns Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-130.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Frankfurt an der Oder. On arrival he finds Glenck has left and Leixner is away. Nothing has been done yet. He has agreed with M. Bernhard (Meyer Bernhard) that he will settle the Betsche (Pszczew) matter, that the estates stay in the Prince's name, and that Leixner takes Kaemen (Kamionna) in the Prince's or Triebenfeld's name. Leixner is in difficulty over the Incolat and Graf Schulenburg; he is content if Triebenfeld lends his name. Triebenfeld sent an estafette after Glenck and goes to Berlin today. He will return Saturday, then go to Betsche, then come to the Prince. Johanni is near. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Noch nichts geschehen, einer traut dem anderen nicht
Abkommen mit Meyer Bernhard: Pszczew-Sache, Güter auf Namen des Fürsten

oe1bu9454-131.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. He has made enquiries in Berlin and says the reports there are lies. On the 20th he means to go back to Frankfurt, settle with Leixner over Kemen (Kamionna) and secure the money needed for Koschentin (Koszęcin). He will prepare the ground so the Prince gets "Koltzig" (doubtful) or the loan. He thinks there is more hope for the estates than for money, because the King does not want to give money away and Russia wants war. In the Broniewski affair the arrest is to be accepted once the causae arresti are proven. The rest (2000 rt, Mell[itz?] and Glenck) is garbled. Nothing here concerns Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-132.notes: The letter is signed v Triebenfeld and written to "Mein Theuerster Freund". The header lists the sender as not identified, so the summary calls him "der Schreiber". After waiting in vain for Glenck in Frankfurt he is going back to Breslau. He complains that people are profiting from the Prince at Betsche (Pszczew) and want the same at Kaemen (Kamionna). He asks the friend to get Director Stubenrauch to buy the estates. He sets out valuations: 10000 Rthl a year in revenue, a capital of 200000 or 250000 Rthl, and the Prince would be content with 180000 Rthl. He also gives figures for Hufe payments. Last, he asks the friend to act on the Koltzig/compensation matter, and to be careful with the Cabinets Rath. Nothing here concerns Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Der Schreiber reist unverrichteter Dinge nach Wrocław zurück, weil er vergeblich auf Glenck gewartet hat.
Er klagt, bei Pszczew hätten andere 30000 Rthl am Fürsten gewonnen.
Der Freund soll Director Stubenrauch zum Kauf von Kamionna bewegen und das Geld bis Johanni beschaffen.
claims.why: Das Geld soll laut Zeilen 49-50 Stubenrauch bis Johanni hergeben, nicht der Freund. Der Freund soll ihn nur dazu bewegen.

claims.statement: Der Schreiber will für 10000 Rthl jährliche Revenue haften.

Ohne Einstandsgeld zahlten die Unterthanen 50 Rthl pro Hufe jährlich.
Wegen des Koltziger Entschädigungsgeschäfts mahnt er zur Vorsicht beim Cabinets Rath.
claims.why: Der Brief nennt die 'Koltziger Güter Sache oder' das 'Dedomagirungs Geschäft' als zwei Möglichkeiten und bittet den Freund dort um sein Bestes. Die Mahnung zur Vorsicht beim Cabinets Rath begründet er mit seiner Furcht vor diesem Mann, nicht mit einem zusammengelegten Koltziger Entschädigungsgeschäft.

oe1bu9454-133.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Frankfurt an der Oder, where he waited three days for Glenck with no result. He goes through seven points: Glenck can prove nothing; Leixner was frightened by fraud at Betsche (Pszczew); the terms for Kaemen (Kamionna); cancelling the partnership contract with Glenck; the Ordens Cammer; the Harlem purchase; and the 100/m rt loan from the Invaliden Casse. He is going back to Berlin to try to close with Stubenrauch, helped by Amelang. News from Berlin: Beyme presented the Prince's compensation request and advised the King to cancel his debt of over 200000 rt. Köckritz is involved. The Prince would get the command if war comes. Also Russia–Austria alliance, Haugwitz. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-134.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. The Invaliden Casse loan has failed because the Ottosche Taxe was reworked downwards to 78/m rt through Leugnich. Stubenrauch and the Pupillen Collegio are refusing too. Beyme told Amelang that the King would write off the Prince's debts as compensation for the Brzyce goods. Amelang proposed Schlabrendorff's confiscated Kolzig goods instead. Figures given: Zagórów taxed at 124/m, carrying debts of 56000. Kolno and Kamionna taxed at 118000, of which 66/m was awarded to Broniewski. Plans: ask Pliehen in Potsdam, borrow 120/m on Konotop and Zagórów, then dismember the Zagórów and Trąbczyn goods. Glenck is heavily blamed.

oe1bu9454-135.notes: Three copies filed together about selling Kamionna (Kaemen) and Kolno. (1) Kabinets Rath Werner, Berlin 19 May 1804, to a Cammer Director. He claims the 2 pc commission promised in the Prince's Revers because he proposed a buyer in December, and says he has learned the sale was concluded through Kammer Rath Ludolff. He fears Glenck will dispute the claim and asks what the purchase price is. (2) The Revers itself, Breslau 17 Dec 1803, signed by Friedrich Ludwig Fürst zu Hohenlohe. (3) Glenck, 12 May 1804, asking about a loan of 60000 rt as a second mortgage. (4) A note from Stubenrauch, 22 May 1804, returning the papers and declining.

oe1bu9454-138.notes: Amelang writes from Berlin to the Prince about the Broniewski case. He points to a resolution of 25 June on the first attempt at deposition. Triebenfeld had told him the Prince would also deposit a caution so as to get possession of the estates. Amelang offered it, and it is put at 10000 rthl. Following this, the deposition and something to do with Kolno and Kaemen (Kamionna) were ordered to the Regierung zu Posen. Amelang expects the Prince to welcome this order. The text is rough: fruchtniß, Beygeschlafen, ſaunte, Angeschrey, Räumig and Ehrpfängt are garbled.

oe1bu9454-139.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Posen to the Prince. The Broniewski settlement (Vergleich) cannot be undone. Glenck submitted it for approval on the 6th. The Prince's protest arrived on the 8th, was set aside, and the settlement was approved and sent to court. Melzer and Glenck each blame the other, or Wunster. Melzer admits that a deposition would have beaten Broniewski. Triebenfeld is going to Betsche. In the Bornstädt affair the court sued for eviction without fixing a liquidum, as it had with the Trąbczyn people. He will come back to evict Bornstädt and check Broniewski's caution. Glenck arrives but has no excuse. Melzer expects the liquidation suit to take 6 to 8 years.

oe1bu9454-140.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Betsche (Pszczew) to the Prince and sends this by express. The sale of Pszczew to the Gemeinden and the Frankfurt buyers (Meyer Bernhard, Leixner) has stalled. Rochlitz is stirring up the settlers with a contract his relative Klein holds. Glenck is intriguing, and the tenant Bornstädt has to be dealt with. Triebenfeld asks for a revers from v. Brandenstein and wants Glenck ordered to hand over the contracts. He asks what to say about the 1000 Friedrichsd'or promised to Bornstädt. Glenck has talked Meyer Bernhard out of paying 66/m Rthl in Posen. Nothing can be done yet about dividing up Kamionna and Kolno. Trąbczyn is not mentioned.

oe1bu9454-141.notes: Triebenfeld, laid up in Posen with gall fever, writes to the Prince about the Broniewski affair. The settlement (Vergleich) that has been concluded gives no security. Redoing it needs Broniewski's wife, who is in Kollo or Warschau. He calls Wunster a scoundrel who colludes with Broniewski and Guderian and pushed the bad settlement through Glenck. Meyer Bernhard and Simon want to pay 6000 instead of 13000 rt. His plan: Broniewski gives security, Glenck presses for 66000 rt to be deposited with Melzer, Broniewski hands over the estates, then Broniewski takes his 53000 rt and Glenck the 13000 for the Prince. There was an attempted seizure (Pfändung) in Betsche; he aims at 30000 rt from Betsche. He defends his openness towards Glenck. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-142.notes: Triebenfeld, sick in Breslau, writes to the Prince. Bornstädt means to leave (the enclosed letter says so). T. asked Glenck to bring the lease and settlement contracts with Bornstädt and got back a curt note (the word describing it is doubtful). He asks the Prince to order Glenck to send the contracts, settlements and accounts, and to write that out of special grace he will give Bornstädt 5000 rt to end everything. An adviser's opinion ("des Brauns Gutachten", unclear) says Bornstädt would need 7500 rt, not counting the honorarium promised in the Betsche (Pszczew) purchase. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-143.notes: Amelang in Berlin writes a short reply to the Prince. He thanks him for being told how the Prince's compensation matter (Entschädigungs Angelegenheit) turned out. The Prince has said he is satisfied with how it ended, so Amelang is left only with a wish (the word is garbled as "Würch") about the King's continued favour. Lines 14-15 are garbled. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Amelang dankt für die Nachricht vom Ausgang der Entschädigungsangelegenheit des Fürsten.

claims.statement: Der Fürst erklärt sich mit dem Abschluss zufrieden; für Amelang bleibt nichts weiter übrig.
claims.why: Dass der Fürst zufrieden ist, steht in den Zeilen 8-10. Zeile 11 geht aber weiter: 'kein Würch [vermutlich Wunsch] weiter übrig als der, daß...'. Der Satz handelt also von einem verbleibenden Wunsch, der die Gnade des Königs betrifft. Dass Amelang 'nichts weiter zu tun' bleibt, ist eine Fehldeutung.

In Trąbczyn werden Befehle gegen seinen Plan gegeben: 100 Scheffel Korn verliehen, Äcker besät. Er will hinfahren, sobald der Wagen fertig ist.

oe1bu9454-146.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Trąbczyn to the Prince. A letter from Pankratz, a Mennonite elder, is enclosed: the Mennonites want to buy the Zagórów and Trąbczyn estates as a whole. Triebenfeld will travel to Lunau. The valuation commission is held up by Glenck's contract of 5 Sept (300 Morgen of demesne land), by his sale of the Komornitzen in Wrąbczyn to v Malachowski, and by a protest from the Gemeinde. He asks for Glenck's reverses and for the contracts of the miller's wife and of the Swięcia Hauländer. He also complains about the fields having been sown, about the surveyors, Wollenhaupt and Landrath v Blomberg. He has lodged an objection to a 6500 rt execution in the Przespolewski matter. Postscript on Radzinski and the disordered registry.

The postscript complains about Glenck's reproaches and his orders on the spot, and reports that the Justiz Bürgermeister (written "Schema", i.e. Schenck) asks for instructions about the Wrąbczyn lands.

oe1bu9454-149.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Trąbczyn to the Prince. He is waiting for settlers from the Oder and Netze Brüche and has sold waste plots at the border. He has quarrelled with Glenck, has had colic, and has trouble with the Oleśnica Erbpächter. The Wrąbczyn subjects refuse their Zins and complain that Glenck threatened to take their plots, that Glenck's Schreiber forced them to serve and that the Meyer hired 18 of them out to Zagorowo burghers at 4 gg a day. oe1bu9454-150.notes: This is a file note, not a letter. It abstracts a letter from Landesältester v. Lichnowski dated 23 Nov 1804 to the Prince (Sr Durchl.). Lichnowski claims 5572 rthl 12 gg of arrears on interest covering 4 May 1803 to 4 Nov. He obtained a mandate from the Kalisz government requiring payment within 14 days. That deadline has passed, so he threatens to apply for sequestration, though he hopes to stay on good terms and expects funds by Christmas. The draft answer, dated 27 Nov 1804, says the tenants have not paid and that he will be satisfied once Triebenfeld has put things in order. Line 6 'admiuhträt' is garbled (probably 'administrirt'). Line 11 'abwägerne' is probably 'aber gerne' and line 13 'Selittel' probably 'Mittel'.

oe1bu9454-153.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince about raising the 25000 Rthl. Herr von Stein, now President of the Bank, has again forbidden all discounting. With Amelang he is trying to get the 25000 Rthl as a stopgap. He reports that business in general is at a standstill, that the Wittwen Casse and Pupillen Collegio are under pressure from threatened bankruptcies in Südpreußen, and that the King is asking where the millions sent there went. oe1bu9454-162.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kalisz to the Prince. A new order from the General Finanz Departement stops the chambers from revising court valuations (Taxen) without its approval. He blames Prinz George and Krieges Rath Korn, who was to revise valuations he had made himself. President v Goldbeck has asked Berlin for permission; Triebenfeld sent this by Estaffette and asked Amelang to push it. Meanwhile he will submit the dismemberment plans. Goldbeck reproached him about the Starostey Strehlitz; they made it up. Goldbeck wants three busts and a Lavoir, which the Prince is asked to buy and send. Through Hussarzewski the Oleśnica matter has gone back to the Patrimonial Gericht. He will calm Lichnowski.

claims.statement: Ein neuer Befehl des General Finanz Departements verbietet den Kammern Revisionen gerichtlicher Taxen ohne dessen Vorwissen.
Triebenfeld führt ihn auf Prinz George und Krieges Rath Korn zurück.
Er hofft auf die Erlaubnis, die Präsident v Goldbeck beantragt hat und die Amelang in Berlin betreiben soll.
Er will die Dismembrationspläne einreichen.
Der Fürst soll für Goldbeck drei Büsten und ein Lavoir kaufen und schicken.
Die Olesnicer Sache ist durch Hussarzewski an das Patrimonialgericht zurückgegangen.

doubtful_words.note: Garbled word. From the context it probably means something like 'unfriendly' or 'cool'.
Possibly a misread name, perhaps Ludolff.
The edition's closing formula is 'In tiefster Ehrfurcht ersterbe', but the writer's own wording varies, so this is not corrected.

oe1bu9454-163.notes: Triebenfeld schreibt aus Kalisz an den Fürsten. Die Antwort an die Olesnicer ist zugestellt, morgen ist Termin in Trąbczyn. Otocki will Szetlewek in Erbpacht nehmen und die Propination beider Güter pachten, laut PS außerdem 20 bis 30 Hufen wie die Colonisten. Tietz soll die alten Bauern in Swincin auskaufen. Honrichs zahlt nicht; Meierowitz würde nach Aufhebung von dessen Contract kaufen. Grimm bietet für Witów. Klage gegen Szczucki und Czizewski in der Przespolewskischen Sache. Der alte Lichnowski bittet um 1390 rth. Beschwerde über den Kammer President; Lavoir und Büsten sollen geschickt werden. Das Gallenfieber ist zurück.

claims.statement: Termin in Trąbczyn in der Olesnicer Sache
Olesnicer hatten mit dem Landrath protestiert, um die 10000 Rthl nicht zu zahlen, und lenken nun ein
Otocki will Szetlewek für 10000 Rthl Bestandsgeld und 1500 Rthl Canon in Erbpacht nehmen
Otocki will die Propination beider Güter pachten
Otocki will 20 bis 30 Hufen in Erbpacht nehmen und wie die Colonisten zahlen
Honrichs zahlt nicht; nach Aufhebung des Contracts würde Meierowitz kaufen
Grimm bietet 2000 Rthl für Witów
Szczucki und Czizewski sollen verklagt werden
Der alte Lichnowski bittet um 1390 Rthl

doubtful_words.note: vielleicht Swięcia; Tietz vielleicht Carl Titz

oe1bu9454-164.notes: Triebenfeld to Hohenlohe, from Kalisz. There is still no resolution from Berlin. He blames the new revision of the Taxen on Prinz George and Kalckreuth, and will have the Landrath attest the Taxen instead. Otocki promises 10000 Rthl plus 2000 rt of Propination rent in advance. If Honrichs is removed, Meierowitz will pay 20000 rtl and a 500 rthl Canon. Buyers want Huben once the land is broken up; he is pressing for the Consens. A Kammer edict of 23 Dec 1803 limits Erbpacht; Glenck kept it quiet and the Olesnicer contract of 22 Febr 1804 was concluded anyway. Dombrowski reports the Prusimski Compromiss and receipts in the Kowaler Archiv. Postscript about busts.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld wartet auf die Berliner Resolution
führt die neue Taxenrevision auf Prinz George und Kalckreuth zurück
Otocki verspricht 10000 Rthl und 2000 Rthl Propinationspacht im Voraus
Meierowitz würde nach Honrichs' Abgang 20000 Rthl und 500 Rthl jährlichen Canon zahlen
Ein Kammeredikt verbot die Erbpacht an Nichtadlige ohne königlichen Consens
Glenck habe dies verschwiegen und den Contract mit den Olesnicern schließen lassen
Laut Dombrowski liegen der Prusimskische Compromiss und Quittungen über Prusimskis Zahlung im Archiv

doubtful_words.note: inflected form of Kalckreuth (line 18); may be a misreading
unclear; perhaps a name or title

oe1bu9454-165.notes: A. Hahn writes from Breslau on 8 March 1805 to Krieges und Forst Rath von Triebenfeld. On the Prince's orders he adds a postscript to the princely letter already posted: he encloses an extract copy of news received from Glenck by today's riding post. He reports that the Prince's health is improving (the attack moved from the right hand to the left foot, and the pain stopped overnight). Bergrath Bernhardi has arrived but is unwell, and the Prince sent Hahn to reassure him. Hahn wishes Triebenfeld a recovery. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Nachtrag im Auftrag des Fürsten zum schon abgesandten fürstlichen Schreiben, Auszug aus Glencks Post in Abschrift beigelegt
Fürst hält es für nützlich
Gesundheit des Fürsten besser, Anfall von rechter Hand in linken Fuß, Schmerz nachts aufgehört
Bergrath Bernhardi angekommen, aber krank; Hahn vom Fürsten zu ihm geschickt, um ihn zu beruhigen
claims.why: Im Brief steht 'Burgrath', nicht 'Bergrath'. Der Titel ist also gedeutet. Außerdem heißt es nur 'nicht ganz gesund' bzw. 'fortdauernde Unpäßlichkeit', nicht 'krank'. Dass der Fürst Hahn zur Beruhigung schickte, ist belegt.

claims.statement: Wunsch für Triebenfelds Genesung

oe1bu9454-166.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Trąbczyn to the Prince. Minister Voss had the dismemberment (parcelling and sale) at Trąbczyn stopped and sent a Cammer commission to check it. Triebenfeld won: the inhibition was withdrawn and net revenues were set at 31000 Rthl. Once the finance department confirms this, credit of 3 to 400000 Rthl will be possible, and the 180850 Rthl still to come in can pay off debts. Buyers had run away when the inhibition became known. He is worn out, has lost 19500 Rthl on his own estates (Schweinern, Kontop), and must go there. Schenck and a few others are to collect the money meanwhile.

claims.statement: Minister Voss ließ die Dismembration in Trąbczyn inhibieren
Die Kommission bestätigte Triebenfelds Nachweise und nahm die Inhibition zurück
Die reinen Jahreseinkünfte wurden auf 31000 Rthl festgestellt
Nach der Konzession hofft er auf Kredit von 3 bis 400000 Rthl
Die ausstehenden 180850 Rthl sollen zur Schuldentilgung dienen
Die Käufer sind nach Bekanntwerden der Inhibition abgesprungen
Eigene Verluste von 19500 Rthl zwingen ihn nach Świniary und Konotop
Schenck soll inzwischen die Gelder einnehmen

doubtful_words.note: the usual closing formula is 'In tiefster Ehrfurcht ersterbe'; this may be misread, or the writer's own wording

oe1bu9454-167.notes: A. Hahn, who serves the Prince ("meinen gnädigsten Herren"), writes from Öhringen to Krieges und Forst Rath von Triebenfeld. He is covering an enclosed letter. The Prince was about to drive to church with "dem alten Herrn" and told Hahn to send it with his regards. He would have written himself, but the courier (Ordonanz) leaves within the hour. The old Prince is very well for his age and shows great attachment to Hahn's master. Postscript: the return to Breslau is fixed for the 25th. Nothing about Trąbczyn. The text is sound. Nothing needs a provable correction.

claims.statement: Hahn übersendet auf Befehl des Fürsten, der mit dem alten Herrn zur Kirche fährt, einen beiliegenden Brief mit dessen Empfehlung.
Der Fürst hätte selbst geschrieben, doch die Ordonanz geht in einer Stunde ab.
Der alte Fürst ist für sein Alter sehr wohl und zeigt viel Attachement für Hahns Herrn.
Die Rückkunft nach Wrocław ist unfehlbar auf den 25. bestimmt.

doubtful_words.note: Possibly meant to be 'Rath' in the address formula; the genitive-looking -s may be the writer's own form.

oe1bu9454-168.notes: Triebenfeld reports to the Prince from Trąbczyn. Snow is holding up his work there. He has concluded contracts with the old peasants, is negotiating with v. Otocki over Szetlewek and the propination, and has good news from Amelang about the loan. Consent to the dismembration is expected. He complains of Glenck, Wollenhaupt, the three Oleśnica men and a Meyer, who are working against him. Claims for surveying and other costs total 3011 rt; he answers Wollenhaupt's claim with counter-claims. Schenck's demands. Postscript: the old subjects of Swięcia bought out, and a new contract for 28 Hufen.

claims.statement: Verträge mit den alten Bauern und Sicherung der Abgaben gerichtlich abgeschlossen
Verhandelt mit v. Otocki über Szetlewek und die Propination
Amelang verspricht Hilfe beim Anlehen
Konsens zur Dismembration erwartet
Glenck, Wollenhaupt, die drei Oleśnicaer und ein Meyer reden Käufern ab
Forderungen von insgesamt 3011 Rthl
Gegenforderungen an Wollenhaupt, er müsse 400 Rthl herausgeben
Swięcia: alte Untertanen ausgekauft, neuer Vertrag über 28 Hufen zu 400 Rthl je Hufe und 15 Rthl jährlichem Zins

oe1bu9454-169.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Kalisz. Minister Voss has forbidden any revision of the Taxen. Triebenfeld is waiting for Amelang's answer on whether the Landrath's revision will be accepted. The dismembration application is in, and the President is sending a Rath to Zagórów and Trąbczyn. He has closed a deal with Meierowitz and wants Honrichs out. Radzinski offers 48000 Rthl in all for Szetlewek; they still disagree about pasture. There are plans for Oleśnica and the Propination, and he hopes for 80000 Rthl by July. Amelang is angry because Goldstücker ceded the Glenck mortgage to Oppenheimer, who refuses to yield priority. The Przespolewski matter will end well. Complaints about Glenck, Sprengel and Chwalowski follow.

claims.statement: Voss hat Revision der Taxen untersagt
wartet auf Amelangs Antwort zur landrätlichen Revision
Rat soll für Dismembration Zagórów und Trąbczyn besichtigen
Abschluss mit Meierowitz
claims.why: Zeile 16 bestätigt den Abschluss mit 'dH. Meierowitz'. Einen Vornamen nennt der Brief nicht. Die Zusammenfassung fügt 'Franz' hinzu.

claims.statement: Radzinski bietet für Szetlewek, 1700 Morgen, zusammen 48000 Rthl; Streit um Weide
claims.why: Angebot, 48000 rt, 1700 Morgen und der Streit um die Weide stehen im Brief. Der Brief sagt aber nur 'Radzinski'. 'Ignatz von' ist hinzugefügt.

claims.statement: hofft bis Juli auf 80000 Rthl
Amelang lärmt wegen Oppenheimers Verweigerung der Priorität der Glenckschen Hypothek auf Oleśnica

doubtful_words.note: possibly Weigel, but it could be a different person

oe1bu9454-170.notes: A. Hahn writes from Breslau to Triebenfeld. The Prince had ordered him to ride to Triebenfeld's own estate Schweinern (Świniary) and warn the Amtmann Käufer and the Förster Bezold, as Triebenfeld asked in doc 174, where the forester is called Peltzold. The forester asked who had denounced him and said he was doing his utmost. Hahn then found the Amtmann in Breslau, who said the same, pointed to his testimonials and good name, and said he could face an investigation calmly. At the end Hahn says something ("Wüsten", probably Büsten) is going off by the fahrende Post. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Auf Befehl des Fürsten ritt Hahn nach Triebenfelds Erbgut Świniary, um mit dem Amtmann Käufer und dem Förster Bezold zu reden.
Er ermahnte den Förster zu Rechtschaffenheit; der Förster fragte, wer ihn beim Fürsten angeschwärzt habe.
Der Förster versicherte, alle Kräfte für das herrschaftliche Interesse einzusetzen.
Den Amtmann traf er in Breslau; dieser erwiderte dasselbe, verwies auf beste Zeugnisse und seinen guten Namen und sieht einer Untersuchung ruhig entgegen.

doubtful_words.note: doc 174 has 'Peltzold'; the name form is uncertain
a word seems to be missing after 'von' (e.g. Triebenfeld or 'Ihnen')

oe1bu9454-171.notes: A. Hahn writes from Erfurt to Triebenfeld with news of the Prince (Sr Durchlaucht). The Prince's foot is nearly healed: only slightly swollen and no longer painful. He is pleased with the Andreas Orden and even more with the courteous manner of the Emperor (Kayser), who is also said to have spoken very flatteringly of him in Breslau. The Hohenlohe regiment marched through today and the Prince rode out to meet it. The Duke of Weimar is expected tomorrow. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Hahn berichtet, dass der Fürst am Fuß fast geheilt und sonst wohlauf sei; der Fuß nur wenig geschwollen, ohne Schmerzen.
Der Andreas Orden habe Freude bereitet, mehr noch das artige Benehmen des Kaysers, von dem der Fürst bezaubert sei.
Auch in Wrocław soll der Kayser schmeichelhaft vom Fürsten gesprochen haben.
Das Regiment Hohenlohe marschierte durch Erfurt, der Fürst ritt ihm entgegen.
Der Herzog von Weimar werde erwartet.

doubtful_words.note: Probably 'Übel' (ailment of the foot); not proven

oe1bu9454-172.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Trąbczyn about the dismembration (the parcelling of the estate into plots). The main hearing is postponed to Monday, when he expects to sign contracts for all plots. He quotes a letter from President v. Goldbeck to Minister Voss: the Kammer has already consented, the Departements Rath zur Höllen made errors, and Goldbeck promises to put them right. He also reports on the Oleśnica men (Kunckel taken into custody), expects a hard day tomorrow over Szetlewek, and says the Winnicki heirs are suing for 1300 rt. He asks the Prince to have tables and fruit trees taken to the President and hopes Amelang's dealings go well.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld betreibt in Trąbczyn die Dismembration, hat den Haupttermin auf Montag verschoben und will dann die Contracte über alle Gründe abschließen.
Goldbeck an Voss: Die Kammer habe bereits eingewilligt, Krieges Rath zur Höllen habe Fehler begangen, die berichtigt werden sollen.
claims.why: The consent (lines 17-18) and the errors (lines 21-22) are stated. But the correction is only a promise to fix the errors 'nach Möglichkeit', and only if Voss grants consent to the dismembration (lines 26-29).

claims.statement: Kunckel von den Olesnicern ist in Verwahrung gebracht.
Wegen Szetlewek erwartet Triebenfeld einen schweren Tag.
Die Winnickischen Erben klagen auf 1300 Rthl Vermessungskosten.
Bitte, 6 Tische und 30 Obstbäume an den Präsidenten fahren zu lassen.

doubtful_words.note: probably 'nimmt' ('nimmt sich jezt noble und brav')

oe1bu9454-173.notes: Triebenfeld an den Fürsten. Punctation Rochlitz/Honrichs über Witów und Rochlitz' Vollmacht sollen laut Glenck im Trąbczyner Archiv liegen; Tietz und Schenck finden nichts; der Fürst soll Glenck anweisen, sonst droht der Verlust von 14000 Rthl. Amelang zu den Taxen; Blomberg verlangt 1000 Rthl voraus. Am Montag Revision in Trąbczyn mit einem Kammerrat nach den Dismembrationsplänen, danach Concession. Erwartet werden 50000+200000+100000=350000 Rthl. Szetlewek soll diese Woche erledigt werden, Oleśnica ist eingeleitet, Propination an den Meistbietenden. 8 neue Dörfer, der Fürst soll Namen schicken. Vertrag mit Schenck liegt bei: 5 Huben und Ernennung des Actuarius beanstandet. Dazu eine Gehaltsrechnung.

claims.statement: Bitte, Glenck zur Beschaffung der Punctation Rochlitz/Honrichs über Witów und der Vollmacht anzuweisen
Im Trąbczyner Archiv nichts gefunden
sonst drohe Verlust von 14000 Rthl
Revision des Locale in Trąbczyn mit Kammerrat nach Dismembrationsplänen
insgesamt 350000 Rthl erhofft
Szetlewek diese Woche erledigen
Namen für 8 neue Dörfer erbeten
Vertrag mit Schenck beiliegend, 5 Huben Land und Ernennung des Actuarius beanstanden

oe1bu9454-174.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Kalisz. The start is missing: the letter opens mid-argument, working out that a Justitiarius who also serves as Rendant would cost nothing, given the savings and rising Sporteln. He complains that his own estate at Schweinern (Świniary) is going to ruin and asks the Prince to send Hahn to warn the Amtmann Käufer and the Förster Peltzold. Hahn's letter of 19 March carries this out. He asks that 1390 rt be sent to Lichnowski. Buyers in Trąbczyn are waiting for Huben of land. He returns Amelang's letter and suggests a text for the Prince to write to the patron about 100/m and 50/m. His cousin Wiesolowski reports on Russian troop numbers. The postscript about busts is garbled.

claims.statement: Ein Justitiarius, der auch den Posten eines Rendanten übernimmt, bringe durch Ersparnisse so viel ein, wie Schenck erhält; die Sporteln würden auf wenigstens 1200 Rthl steigen
Bittet, Hahn nach Świniary zu schicken, um Amtmann Käufer und Förster Peltzold zu verwarnen
In Trąbczyn warten Kaufwillige auf etliche Huben Land gegen Barzahlung
Bittet, Lichnowski die 1390 Rthl zu schicken
claims.why: Line 30 is garbled ('Habe Ewr Durchlaucht den im Lichnowski die 1390 rt geschickt') and reads more like a question whether the money was sent. Calling it a request is an interpretation.

claims.statement: Sendet Amelangs Brief zurück
Wiesolowski berichtet von russischen Truppen, zusammen über 300/m Mann

doubtful_words.note: Probably 'werden' ('darf mehr gehalten werden'), but it may be the writer's own slip.
Hahn's letter (doc. 170) writes 'bezold'; the correct form is uncertain.
The postscript in lines 67-71 is garbled.

oe1bu9454-175.notes: Hahn, who writes from the Prince's household in Breslau, sends Triebenfeld two papers on the Prince's orders: one an original, the other a copy. The Prince asks for Triebenfeld's opinion on what to do in these matters. Girard and Haugk[?] are pressing hard. The Prince would send the sum at once to satisfy them, if his funds had not been drained by the journey. "Lasserwelche" is garbled (probably "Casse, welche"). The letter says nothing about Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Hahn übersendet auf Befehl zwei beiliegende Schriftstücke, ein Original und eine Abschrift
claims.why: Z. 4-6 sprechen von einem Befehl, zwei Stücke zu übersenden, eines das Original, eines die Abschrift. Wessen Befehl das ist, sagt der Brief nicht. Die Zusammenfassung schreibt 'im Auftrag des Fürsten', das ist eine Deutung.

claims.statement: Der Fürst bittet um Triebenfelds Meinung, was zu tun sei
Besonders Girard drängt
Der Fürst würde die erforderliche Summe sofort schicken, wären seine Mittel durch die Reise nicht erschöpft

doubtful_words.note: Probably 'Casse, welche' (the Prince's funds), but garbled.
Doubtful name reading; not used in the summary.
The word 'auf' or 'zufolge' may be missing (e.g. 'habe auf dem Befehl').

oe1bu9454-176.notes: Hahn writes from Breslau to Triebenfeld. An express courier has brought news that the reigning Prince of Hohenlohe-Neuenstein has died. He took ill on 24 July and died of a stroke on 27 July. Under his will Hahn's "gnädigster Fürst" is sole heir, and possession was taken at once in Öhringen and the other places. The Princes of Langenburg and Kirchberg tried measures based on a partition treaty; their troops were turned back and the Ingelfingen patents posted. The Prince will travel there in September after the Silesian reviews. Because he will be away a long time, he leaves the South Prussian affairs to Triebenfeld. Rough transcription: several words are garbled.

claims.statement: Hahn meldet den Tod des regierenden Fürsten zu Hohenlohe-Neuenstein am 27. Juli durch Schlagfluss
Laut Testament ist Hahns Fürst Alleinerbe; in Öhringen und den übrigen Orten wurde sofort Besitz ergriffen
Maßnahmen der Fürsten zu Langenburg und Kirchberg, gestützt auf einen Teilungsvertrag, wurden abgewehrt, ihre Truppen zurückgewiesen
Der Fürst will im September nach den schlesischen Revuen dorthin reisen
Er überlässt die südpreußischen Angelegenheiten Triebenfelds Einsicht, da er lange abwesend sein wird

doubtful_words.note: probably 'beygehen lassen' = presumed; also 'welche anzuschlagen' unclear

oe1bu9454-177.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Berlin during the Prussian mobilisation. Voss and Klewitz are away, so little can be done. Reinbeck is pushing the approval of the dismemberment (the new colonies at Zagórów and Trąbczyn), and the loans from the Invaliden Casse and the Pupillen Collegium depend on it. Political news follows. Enclosures: proposed names for the new villages, and list B of the colonies (21407 Morgen, 578 Wirthe; 4575 Morgen stay with the Dominium). Money: 7130 rt received; Radzinski owes 6000; the scattered colonists and a would-be tenant promise payments; Prusimska 20000, Weigel 23000 and Schlabrendorff 25000 rt still to pay. Postscript: 2000 rt paid to Obrist v Schlieben; he has not yet been able to speak to Hardenberg.

claims.statement: Wegen der Mobilmachung ist in Berlin wenig zu erreichen.
Reinbeck betreibt die Approbation der Dismembration bei Zagórów und Trąbczyn.
Davon hängt das erhoffte Geld von Invaliden Casse und Pupillen Collegium ab.
Verzeichnis der neuen Kolonien: 21407 Morgen, 578 Wirthe; dem Dominium bleiben 4575 Morgen.
Radzinski soll 6000 Rthl erlegen.
Zerstreute Colonisten versprachen etliche Tausend Rthl.
Zu zahlen bleiben Prusimska 20000, Weigel 23000, Schlabrendorff 25000 Rthl.

oe1bu9454-178.notes: Hahn writes to Triebenfeld from Dresden. He has found, among his papers, some chartes blanches signed by the Prince that were meant for Triebenfeld and were packed in haste. He apologises: in the last nights before leaving he got no rest, because Cammer Director Graf arrived and all Hohenlohe business had to be settled before the journey. He sent the other chartes blanches to the Fräulein von Triebenfeld. In a postscript he says the Prince has named him Expeditions Rath. Nothing about Trąbczyn. Several words are garbled: Eilrigbreslau, Behringen, ankand, angrenge.

claims.statement: Hahn hat unter seinen Papieren noch von Sr Durchlaucht unterschriebene chartes blanches gefunden, die für Triebenfeld bestimmt waren
Er entschuldigt das Versehen: In den letzten Nächten vor der Abreise sei der Cammer Director Graf eingetroffen, alles Hohenlohische musste vor der Reise erledigt werden
Die übrigen chartes blanches hat er an die Fräulein von Triebenfeld geschickt
Der Fürst hat ihn vor der Abreise zum Expeditions Rath ernannt
claims.why: Der Brief schreibt nur 'Sr. Durchl.' und nennt keinen Titel 'Fürst'. Das ist eine Deutung, deshalb auf den Wortlaut des Briefs zurückgeführt.

oe1bu9454-179.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. The dismembration and the Betsche matter have been approved by the King. The Kalisz chamber's valuations put the yield of the estates at 40260 Rthl. Debts total 698000 Rthl. With General v. K[öckritz] he plans to ask the King for Tresorscheine to pay them, the matter to be pursued by Hoff Fiscal Pochammer, for whom he asks the Prince to sign a power of attorney quickly. Glenck: he knows nothing of the Prusimska matter and wants consent to sell his lands; Triebenfeld promised him 8000 Rthl sub spe rati to buy them back. He advises against consent for Santomisl (Betsche). He sees no way to raise the 30000 Rthl and complains about the other mandatories.

claims.statement: Dismembration und Pszczew-Sache vom König genehmigt
Kalischer Kammer setzte den Ertrag auf 40260 Rthl fest
claims.why: Z. 20-25: Die Taxen der Kalischen Kammer sind beendet; der Ertrag von 40260 rthl ist im Attest des General Finanz Departements festgesetzt, nicht von der Kammer.

claims.statement: Schulden 698000 Rthl
mit General v. Köckritz Tresorscheine vom König erbitten
Pochammer soll die Sache betreiben, Vollmacht eilig erbeten
Glenck weiß nichts von der Prusimska-Sache
8000 Rthl sub spe rati für den Rückkauf der Gründe zugesagt
rät vom Consens für Santomisl ab
keine Möglichkeit für die 30000 Rthl

doubtful_words.note: garbled passage on the hereditary buyers in Zagorowo and Trąbczyn

oe1bu9454-179a.notes: Group of copied enclosures (179a) about a debt-relief plan for Zagórów and Trąbczyn. A: summary of revenues from the Kalisz Kammer (Kalisz, 28 March 1806; Mencke, v Hellen), net 40260 rthl 14 g 11 d. B: list of the Prince of Hohenlohe's debts, total 698784 rt including the Courland debt. C: draft memorial to the King (Berlin, 25 April 1806), signed v Triebenfeld, asking for 698000 rt in Tresorscheine secured on the estates, with an amortisation fund of 34000 Rthl a year. D: amortisation plan. Then a fragment of a power of attorney. Sender and recipient are given as not identified; only the signature on the memorial names Triebenfeld.

claims.statement: Kammerübersicht der Revenuen von Zagórów und Trąbczyn, reiner Ertrag 40260 Rthl
Honrichs pachtet Vorwerk Trąbczyn für 3000 Rthl
Radzinski auf Szetlewek 1500 Rthl Erbpachts Canon
Passiva des Fürsten insgesamt 698784 Rthl
Lichnowski auf Trąbczyn 42000 Rthl
Protestation für die Prusimska 8333 Rthl
Entwurf einer Eingabe an den König, gezeichnet v Triebenfeld, um 698000 Rthl in Tresorscheinen auf die Güter
Amortisationsfonds 34000 Rthl jährlich
16 neue Dörfer und 500 Familien

oe1bu9454-180.notes: Triebenfeld in Berlin answers the Prince's letters of 8 and 18 April. The creditor Nathan Liepmann's claim is already listed among the known debts. The dismemberment money of about 60,000 rt will come in slowly, so he must keep borrowing. With the Betsche (Pszczew) matter settled, the people are to pay 2,000 rt and Raven 1,200 rt in transfer fees (Laudemien). He will collect at Johanni to raise 30/m rt. The Michaelis matter is for the Betsche subjects to pay. He knows nothing of a Posen miller claiming 1 rt 7 g. If Raven will not pay the fees, the communities are to take the estate back. On the Württemberg encroachments into the Prince's territories, Berlin promises help but he doubts its sincerity. President v Hähneln told him the Prince still suffers from gout, and he urges a fontanelle. He may come to Öhringen once the business is done. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-190.notes: Hahn, the Prince's secretary, writes from Öhringen to Triebenfeld. The Prince is ready to help him and asks Triebenfeld to do the same, by sending the Prince the draft (Schema) of the consent, so that Glenck's complaints stop. If Glenck refuses the conditions again, he is to be left to his ruin. In the extract, Glenck describes his distress over the Wrąbczyn estates. oe1bu9454-191.notes: Triebenfeld to the Prince from Trąbczyn after 5 weeks of gall fever. Lists the debts to be paid from the Justizfond (Oppenheimer, Lichnowski, Prusimska etc.). An execution decree from Posen for the Prusimska dowry claim (about 22000 rt); he gained time in Kalisz with Rapacki's documents. In Trąbczyn: tenants claim war losses; peasants left their assigned grounds, took back old ones, drove off German colonists; floggings at Swiątniki, peasants submit, boundaries drawn. Contracts of Honrichs (now one year, 2800 rt at Christmas), Zglinski (gave up) and Kopojno (1 year, 2500 rt) changed; dismemberment at 600 rt/Hufe. Tietz of Drzewce claims a 600 rt pension. oe1bu9454-194.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Kontop. He is kept from travelling to Sławięcice because the Invaliden Casse has sued him: it gets no interest and wants the whole capital. The hearing is on the 26th. In Poland things go better. The Friedensgericht has decided the vindication of the Trąbczyn estates favourably, and the case has gone to the Tribunal in Kalisz. oe1bu9454-196.notes: Triebenfeld to the Prince. oe1bu9454-200.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. The Prince's letter came with "Hauses häuer" (garbled; they are the "Vögel"). The birds arrive too late for General v. Köckritz, who will have left. Seegebarth is to be told the rest will be settled once money comes from the Polish estates. Brufurt has not come, so T. must find another way to reach Poland and Zagórów, and wants to be back by the 7th. Weigel will probably not accept Stössel as his debtor. T. proposes that Weigel acquire the Silesian estates the Prince takes and satisfy Stössel, arguing that the Prince's estates are entailed (fideicommiss). The King is coming, and T. has asked whether the Prince might show himself to the King in Koźle. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-201.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. Weigel has agreed to take the estates being bargained for in exchange for Zagórów, the Knobelsdorff or Poninski ones. In return he will offset his own and Stössel's claims. He is to come to Schweinern (Świniary) on the 30th to talk it over. Triebenfeld's plan: rich Breslau merchants want to buy estates. Someone has offered 220000 rt cash for Schweinern and he asks 250000. With 90000 intabulated (registered as debt on the estate), 160000 would be left in cash. Once Weigel and Stössel are paid, and Grotowski, Lichnowski and Zerboni are charged to Trąbczyn, 150000 would clear the other debts. He urges the Prince to pursue the plan with F. August.

oe1bu9454-202.notes: A private letter to a "Lieber Freund", signed v Triebenfeld and written at Schweinern (Świniary), dated in the text "20ten Aug 10". The edition dates it 1810-08-30, which fits letter 201's note that Weigel would visit on the 30th. Sender and recipient are marked not identified, so the summary says "der Schreiber". Weigel has visited, left satisfied and put the matter in the writer's hands. He will accept the estates the Fürst is acquiring, and he wants a detailed written plan so he can explain it to his son. A long quoted speech by Weigel praises the writer's lack of self-interest. In a postscript the writer hopes to sell 2 Freystellen quickly. Nothing about Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-205.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. Köckritz has left, and the King is to follow. Weigel would accept being registered on the Bischdorf estates if Stössel takes them, and would then clear Koszęcin. He reports that debts in Poland are to be paid, that war between France and Russia is feared, and a rumour of peace between Russia and Turkey. oe1bu9454-206.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince after Lombardini's visit. He warns of hidden dangers, says the Prince should expect nothing from this government and should hope for satisfaction from the North, and offers to go to Petersburg himself. Knobelsdorff's exchange (Tausch) is going ahead. On the 35/m rt he is waiting for Eberhard's schema. In Cosel Scharnhorst spoke on the Prince's behalf, and a sum of money was offered, which the Prince should refuse. Triebenfeld has to sell something at Petersdorff because his travel is costly. He plans a trip to Poland on the 2nd with a four-point plan for Zagorowo (Cabanis, the contracts, the settlers' payments, Honrichs) and names Sommer and Hegener as helpers. Several lines are garbled (14, 29, 36-37, 44-46).

oe1bu9454-207.notes: This is a copy of a Pro Memoria from Kalisz, signed at line 28 by Hecker and Honrichs (the estate side) and addressed to "Ewr p", presumably the Prince. The metadata identifies neither sender nor recipient, so the summary describes the document by its signatures. It reports four things: the Trąbczyn lawsuit has been started in Kalisz with a hearing on 24 October; the lawyer (name doubtful: Falz[?]) has been paid a 200 Rthl advance; the sequestration has ended; and there is a rumour that the King of Prussia will take back the outstanding money. It then covers a proposed settlement with the Erbpächter of Olesnica (12 Hufen) and the complaints of the peasants and Holländer about grain prices and rent per Morgen. v Triebenfeld's note at lines 30-33 is about remitting arrears, and adds that Knobelsdorff prefers land to interest.

oe1bu9454-208.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. He has not yet travelled to Poland because he has no money. He says prospects look better and mentions a third party besides Knobelsdorff and Strachwitz, but that passage is garbled. In "die Schlieben" matter he was nearly distrained: his Schweinern lease money was arrested and an execution for 48 rt 6 g in costs was sent. Lombardini refused to pay and sent the executor away. Triebenfeld asks the Prince to instruct Lombardini to pay. The rest is news: royal manoeuvres near Potsdam and Berlin, Labaye's offer in Paris of linen and iron for the contribution, colonial goods seized on the Elbe, a rumour of 60000 French troops, 30 arrests in Berlin, and Kalckreuth's standing slipping. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-212.notes: Triebenfeld to the Prince from Swiątniki, 1 January 1811. After a severe illness he reports that nobody pays: 31 lawsuits are pending, and he plans to evict the Olesnicer, Niedźwiecki (Kopojno) and Hawich (Drzewce) and to re-establish 3 Vorwerke. He lists debts (garbled passage). New edicts give colonists 6 free years. He offered colonists remission of interest, which they refuse. Napoleon's declaration on 40-year repayment of debts owed to Prussia has confused everyone. In the Trąbczyn case, after a secret letter from Poniatowski, the tribunal referred the matter to the higher magistracy. The Hauländer offer 40000 rt. There is an Anschlag for the Zagórów estates. He is ill and freezing in a peasant hut.

oe1bu9454-213.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Swiątniki. He has recovered from illness but was hurt when his carriage overturned on the way to Konin. State taxes are paid except 900 t., and he hopes to lift the sequestration soon. He lists the 43 lawsuits against debtors (Niedźwiecki, Nossalski, the Olesnicer, the Wrąbczyn peasants, Berda, the Hauländer, Rybbeck, a miller, and 29 against the Colonisten). He gives expected revenues and his costs, including the Trąbczyn and Meierowitz suits at 750 rt. The sequestor is a favourite of Prefect Garczynski. There are rumours from Berlin: Hardenberg does not know of the new arrest and the 40-year amortisation, and asks for proofs. In the postscript Triebenfeld asks to be written to by express messenger and reports that he has hired 3 lawyers for 700 rt.

oe1bu9454-214.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Kalisz to the Prince. He offers condolences on the death of the Fürstin Sacken and reports the approved Transact: bank and invalid debts are to be paid off over 41¾ years at 6 pct. The minister has hinted at a similar moratorium for private debts, including Weigel. The Erbpächter pay nothing and their contracts are to be cassated, with Vorwerke laid out instead. oe1bu9454-216.notes: Triebenfeld to the Prince from Blizanow. The private debts and the Bayonne sums (bank, invalid and pupil funds) are expected to fall under a 41 3/4-year moratorium. oe1bu9454-217.notes: Von Sanitz writes from Berlin to Triebenfeld, whom he addresses as Lieutenant. He apologises for answering late. He has left Silesia after about 49 years and is in Berlin to try to save his lost fortune. His former lawyer Weltzer has little hope. The foreign department has approached the Dresden court, and the French envoy offers conditional hope. The Saxon court reports that Dąbska petitioned the Emperor and that Polish commissioners ordered the estates returned to her. He asks whether the first Tribunal has given its sentence on the Prince's Trąbczyn estates, and asks for copies of the Friedensrichter ruling and of the tribunal sentence. He adds rumours of war in the North. The text is heavily garbled.

oe1bu9454-218.notes: Triebenfeld (Blizanow) to Prince Hohenlohe. Heuthausen will present reports. Stössel and Weigel are to take Schurgast and the mortgage. If the debts are higher, Triebenfeld would trade Blizanow with Wartensleben's eldest son and add a 30000 rt mortgage on Kontop. He wants a quick, secret answer because Wartensleben is negotiating with Gumperts. oe1bu9454-220.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Brieg. The Prince's letter reached him three weeks late by way of Schweinern. He sold his wool in Ostrów and went to the old Graf Wartensleben in Neisse, but came too late: Wartensleben had already closed a deal over Schurgast with a Kalisz merchant. He now proposes the Constadt estates of the young Wartensleben (asking price 200000, debts 120000). Weigel and Stössel would take these estates together with the Zagórów mortgage and give the Prince a receipt for 350000, which would free Koschentin as a Majorat for Prinz Alexander. He asks for a quick answer to Blizanow, and for the Anschlag and the list of arrears back in the original for the court date in Kalisz. Nothing in the letter concerns Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: Triebenfeld kam beim alten Wartensleben in Nysa zu spät; Skorogoszcz ging für 135000 Rthl an einen Kaufmann aus Kalisz
claims.why: Zu spät und Abschluss mit einem Kaufmann aus Kalisz stimmen. Die 135000 rt sind aber der Wert der Güter, die Wartensleben für Schurgast annimmt (Z. 10). Es ist kein Kaufpreis für Skorogoszcz.

oe1bu9454-221.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Blizanow. He cannot send the 18000 Rthl ordered from the Zagórów estates until two lawsuits are won, and he hopes the Christmas interest can be paid so the moratorium holds. He has started a sale of Zagórów to Stössel through Graf Leopold v Wartensleben, Stössel's son-in-law. He proposes a scheme in which he exchanges Blizanow for Sandrelzki's Pila estates, Weigel and Stössel are paid off (470000 Rthl calculation), and Koszęcin is saved. He rejects Konstadt and Schurgast. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

oe1bu9454-222.notes: Triebenfeld, writing from Blizanow, reports to the Prince that Baron Stössel is willing to take the Zagórów estates for his claims under Triebenfeld's plan. The evidence is an enclosed letter. He urgently asks whether the Prince agrees to settle with Stössel and Weigel this way. In the postscript, Graf Wartensleben has come from Breslau: Stössel will deal together with Weigel, but wants a letter from the Prince. Wartensleben suggests what that letter should say about Koschentin, the mother-in-law's will, and Zagórów, to which Triebenfeld would add the Blizanow estates. A mounted messenger has been sent. Köckritz calls Triebenfeld to Berlin. His eldest son has been appointed to the Garde du Corps. Mostly readable; some words are garbled.
